articles.title: Trump: French language not a factor in Canada trade talks
articles.summary: President Trump said Tuesday that Canada’s French language requirements are not a factor in the escalating trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa, contradicting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. “I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French! In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “This…
articles.body:
President Trump said Tuesday that Canada’s French language requirements are not a factor in the escalating trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa, contradicting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

“I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French! In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing,” Trump wrote on Truth Social . “This lie was made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec. I love French Canadians!”

His comments echo those from U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who told CNBC the Canadian claim that French language requirements were a sticking point was a “funny, fake story.”

Carney said Monday that Canada could not accept Washington’s proposed trade deal given its demands to roll back French language requirements.

“We were ready and close to having a comprehensive agreement that would be fair to both countries. But they made changes, including threats on the French language and Quebec culture and Canadian culture,” the prime minister said during a press conference, speaking in French.

“That is not acceptable. That would never be acceptable,” he added.

Canada’s French language requirements have been considered a trade barrier in the U.S. given the added costs and efforts of redesigning packaging to include French labels.

However, the issue is of paramount importance in Canada, particularly in the province of Quebec, where French is the primary language.

articles.title: Iran vows retaliation after widened US sanctions
articles.summary: Iran threatened to retaliate after the Trump administration on Monday unveiled a new effort to isolate the Islamic Republic from the global economy and ramp up pressure to bring the nearly six-month-long war to a close and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shared few details about “Operation Economic Outcast” in highly…
articles.body:
Iran threatened to retaliate after the Trump administration on Monday unveiled a new effort to isolate the Islamic Republic from the global economy and ramp up pressure to bring the nearly six-month-long war to a close and reopen the Strait of Hormuz .

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shared few details about “Operation Economic Outcast” in highly anticipated remarks following President Trump’s warning last week that he would hit Iran with an “Economic D-Day.”

The secretary called on nations across the world to sever financial ties with the Middle Eastern country or risk being cut out of the U.S. dollar system.

Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh told state television that Iran was “fully prepared for the U.S. sanctions.”

“Our defense is no longer defensive; the enemies should wait for an attack,” the Iranian official said, according to Reuters .

Bessent did not name specific countries on Monday but said broadly that the Trump administration was “giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior.” Additionally, the Treasury Department chief did not provide a timeline for countries to comply with the new directive.

“We’re not going to name names,” he said. “We’ve already seen some results, and I am confident the president, as you all know, is quite persuasive.”

China, the largest buyer of Iranian oil , said Tuesday that new U.S. sanctions “will only further intensify tensions.”

“China’s cooperation with Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined,” Lin Jian, a spokesperson for the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said during a press briefing, according to CNN .

Lin said China is “closely following” developments in the U.S. economic campaign and “will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests.”

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian pushed back Monday against “bullying” from the U.S. during a meeting with Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, according to ISNA news agency.

Pezeshkian said the U.S. “must change its tone” in its negotiations with Iran, which are being mediated by Pakistan, as “reliance on coercion and bullying will only complicate the implementation” of a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the countries in June.

He later stressed that Tehran would “overcome all forms of pressure and threats” from the U.S.

articles.title: What is the US reproductive tourism industry really selling?
articles.summary: So, is the U.S. a nation that helps its people bear children, or one that designs children and sells them to any willing buyer?
articles.body:
Following the Supreme Court’s landmark decision on birthright citizenship, moves to ban foreign nationals from using American surrogates dominated headlines. But lawmakers should not stop there. The U.S. should restrict all forms of reproductive tourism, not just birth-tourism.

Surrogacy is just one branch of a larger reproductive industry. In fact, most reproductive tourists seek in vitro fertilization . Before Congress prunes the branch, it should look at the tree and ask a blunt question: What exactly are we selling?

Strip away the language of “family-building” and “fertility journeys,” and the answer is that reproductive tourism sells the creation and selection of human embryos, the buying and selling of human eggs and sperm, and — thanks to birthright citizenship — potentially an American passport.

The industry’s own data tell the story plainly. A comprehensive study of the national IVF registry found that non-U.S. residents accounted for 59,246 assisted reproductive technology cycles between 2014 and 2022 , arriving from 182 countries. China alone generated 19,718 cycles, nearly three times as many as the next-closest country.

These patients do not use U.S. clinics the way Americans do. Compared with U.S. residents, foreign patients are much more likely to use pre-implantation genetic testing (68 percent versus 43 percent) and donor eggs (52 percent versus 9 percent). An earlier CDC analysis found the same pattern, as the tourist share of cycles more than doubled between 2006 and 2013 .

The international clientele is buying the specific services the rest of the world restricts or bans: advanced IVF technology, genetic screening and selection of embryos and gametes purchased from American donors. The lure of reproductive tourism in the U.S. relies on these ethically fraught aspects of the fertility industry to draw in foreign customers, many of whom cannot access these services abroad.

Britain, for example, abolished donor anonymity because it concluded children have a right to know where they come from. The United Kingdom, Canada, France, and Australia all ban non-medical sex selection in most cases. Italy and Turkey limit their own citizens’ ability to travel for third-party services. Most developed nations prohibit cross-border commercial surrogacy, making the U.S. a major outlier on all accounts.

With essentially no federal or state laws governing these practices beyond the FDA’s infectious-disease screening, services come down to clinic preference. For foreign nationals, the process is relatively straightforward: Apply for a B-2 medical visa or travel authorization, provide proof of medical arrangements and bring sufficient funds. Foreign nationals can even ship their own embryos into the country, classified as “human cells and tissues,” for genetic testing or surrogacy purposes.

So consider each component of the sale honestly.

First, we are selling human embryo creation on an industrial scale. Standard IVF produces more embryos than will ever be transferred, because surplus is efficient for success rates. An estimated 1.5 million human embryos now sit frozen in American storage tanks, a population larger than most American cities, suspended while their progenitors decide whether to implant, donate, discard, or simply stop paying the storage fees. Every reproductive tourist adds to this inventory and then, in many cases, flies home, leaving behind embryos whose fate no American law meaningfully governs.

Second, we are selling selection. Clinics market “family balancing.” to international patients. Couples travel from countries that outlawed the practice of culling embryos by sex and, increasingly, as polygenic screening companies enter the market, by predicted traits. It shifts the focus from infertility or the creation of a child to an emphasis on designing a certain kind of child.

Third, we are selling other people’s bodies and origins. Agencies openly advertise menus of egg donors by height, race (“Asian, Caucasian, African”), SAT score, and Ivy League degree to international clients, a form of catalog shopping for human characteristics that would be instantly recognized as grotesque in any other context. A recent example of this is Alysa Liu, the 2026 Olympic gold medal winner in women’s figure skating, whose Chinese father relied on donor eggs of an American and IVF for her conception, and a separate surrogate-mother for her gestation and birth.

Finally, we are selling citizenship. The Supreme Court ruled in June that the Fourteenth Amendment guarantees citizenship to virtually every child born on American soil. That answers the constitutional question for now and sharpens the policy question: Any foreign national who commissions a birth here is purchasing, along with everything else, a U.S. passport, birth certificate, Social Security Number, and all the benefits of U.S. citizenship.

The clinics are not shy about any of this, either. The California Center for Reproductive Health advertises an international menu listing egg donation, IVF, and “ gender selection ” side by side, with interpreters in Chinese, Russian, German, and Hebrew. Western Fertility Institute in Los Angeles markets itself abroad as a “ one-stop shop .”

San Diego Fertility Center courts patients who struck out under their home countries’ rules, promising beaches alongside the lab work. Pacific Fertility Center runs a dedicated affiliate for Japanese patients and has compressed the required visit to as short as 10 days. New York’s Center for Human Reproduction boasts of an international clientele that barely needs to set foot in the office.

Others offer full concierge packages — airport transfers, hotels, legal coordination — and state the value proposition outright: Not every country offers the same options. Egg donation and gender selection “are often limited or unavailable” where clients live.

These examples underscore how easy it is for foreign nationals to access such services in the U.S., even without a physical presence here.

A nation can take seriously its own infertility crisis without operating an open-borders bazaar in embryos, eggs, and passports for the clientele of the entire world. Indeed, when we encourage the surplus creation of human embryos, sex-selection, genetic grading and international access as mere “human cells and tissues” for paying clients from 182 countries, we are ratifying, in law and in commerce, the proposition that a child can be a product — specified, purchased, and delivered — on the world market.

So, is the U.S. a nation that helps its people bear children, or one that designs children and sells them to any willing buyer? Until we close our reproductive-technology borders, the world is entitled to assume we have given our answer.

Emma Waters is a Policy Analyst in the Center for Technology and the Human Person at The Heritage Foundation.

New York’s Center for Human Reproduction boasts of an international clientele that barely needs to set foot in the office.

Others offer full concierge packages — airport transfers, hotels, legal coordination — and state the value proposition outright: Not every country offers the same options. Egg donation and gender selection “are often limited or unavailable” where clients live.
These examples underscore how easy it is for foreign nationals to access such services in the U.S., even without a physical presence here.

A nation can take seriously its own infertility crisis without operating an open-borders bazaar in embryos, eggs, and passports for the clientele of the entire world. Indeed, when we encourage the surplus creation of human embryos, sex-selection, genetic grading and international access as mere “human cells and tissues” for paying clients from 182 countries, we are ratifying, in law and in commerce, the proposition that a child can be a product — specified, purchased, and delivered — on the world market.

So, is the U.S. a nation that helps its people bear children, or one that designs children and sells them to any willing buyer? Until we close our reproductive-technology borders, the world is entitled to assume we have given our answer.
Emma Waters is a Policy Analyst in the Center for Technology and the Human Person at The Heritage Foundation.

articles.title: China: New US sanctions on Iran ‘will only further intensify tensions’
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Tuesday the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran “will only further intensify tensions” between the two countries. “Economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue. They will only further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks,” Lin told reporters, according to CNN. The Treasury Department announced…
articles.body:
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Tuesday the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran “will only further intensify tensions” between the two countries.

“Economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue. They will only further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks,” Lin told reporters, according to CNN .

The Treasury Department announced Monday it was expanding its authority to sanction individuals involved in five sectors of the Iranian economy: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.

The Treasury Department also sanctioned nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels that “enable the Iranian regime’s recklessness, including illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil‑revenue generation networks,” the department noted in a release .

During a Monday press conference, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent did not call out any specific foreign governments for doing business with the Iranian regime.

“We’re not going to name names. We’ve already seen some results, and I am confident [President Trump], as you all know, is quite persuasive,” Bessent said Monday.

“I would expect that very quickly, if they do not respond, then you will see the ramifications of their actions,” he added.

But China is Iran’s largest trading partner and primary purchaser of its oil exports. Iranian oil exports to China have dropped precipitously during the war, falling to below 800,000 barrels per day last month, Reuters reported .

Lin, the Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, noted his country’s relationship with Iran “should not be disrupted or undermined” by U.S. economic interference.

“China is closely following relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests,” he added, per CNN.

Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet in Washington, D.C., next month, during a state visit by the Chinese leader. The U.S. president is seeking a trade deal with his Chinese counterpart, under which Beijing would boost purchases of American agricultural products, Boeing jets and U.S. oil.

Before and during the Middle Eastern conflict, the Trump administration has sanctioned Chinese entities processing Iranian oil, homing in on small-to-medium teapot refineries.

But China’s Commerce Ministry in May blocked the Treasury’s sanctions on those refineries, arguing they violate international law.

articles.title: Should Taiwan be worried after Trump drops support for South Korea?
articles.summary: Last week, Trump walked back a key element of America’s security commitment to the Indo-Pacific.
articles.body:
President Trump has discovered, painfully, that Iran is no Venezuela.

His brilliantly executed military operation partially decapitating a criminal South American regime could not easily be replicated against a far more powerful adversary in the Mideast — especially when it is actively supported by nuclear-armed China, Russia and North Korea. More ominous than the current Iran stalemate itself, Trump and his advisers have over-learned that geopolitical lesson and misapplied it to other confrontations with America’s enemies.

Last week, Trump walked back a key element of America’s security commitment to the Indo-Pacific. “Based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un, of North Korea,” said Trump, I am not happy with the fact that the United States has, long ago, agreed to participate in Joint Military Exercises with South Korea.”

He directed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to curtail U.S. participation in the exercises the two nations have carried out for decades. The drills are conducted in accordance with the 1954 Mutual Defense Treaty that is identical to the U.S. treaty executed with Taiwan the same year, after the end of the Korean War . Trump indicated it was a form of payback for Seoul’s decision not to participate in the current U.S. operations against Iran .

Trump also said the joint drills are an unnecessary and provocative expense since Kim Jong Un has been “unthreatening and respectful” during his presidency. In one fell swoop, he gave North Korea the major concession Kim, his father, Kim Jong Il, and his grandfather, Kim Il Sung, have sought and been denied by 14 presidential administrations of both parties. Trump did not suggest that the exercise freeze is related to allegations of U.S. munitions shortfalls related to the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine, but both allies and adversaries can conclude that the United States is overstretched in this multifront confrontation.

Two of the most fraught issues in the Indo-Pacific are China’s expansionist and legally unfounded claims to Taiwan and to Scarborough Shoal in the Philippines. Yet neither has been mentioned. It appears that Team Trump is anxious about doing or saying anything that could ruffle leader Xi Jinping’s feathers before his upcoming meeting with Trump in Washington next month.

Badly burned by the Iran misadventure, the administration is now shying away from any moral or even declared policy commitment to support Taiwan against Chinese aggression. In danger of becoming a dead letter is the congressional mandate in the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act, as well as the many other congressional actions meant to protect Taiwan — all of which might fall into what Elbridge Colby, Trump’s policy adviser at the Defense Department, now calls legacy commitments not suitable for today’s “ flexible realism [and] the foreign policy of common sense. “

That new approach hardly describes Trump’s handling of the confrontation with Iran, and ominously suggests that its tragic mistakes have further paralyzed the president’s will to confront Xi, who has somehow ingratiated himself with Trump despite having deceived him on several major issues: the COVID pandemic, honoring trade agreements, support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and providing assistance to Iran.

Colby is presently managing the China-Taiwan portfolio. He as outspoken in questioning U.S. support for Ukraine during the Biden administration, writing in 2024 that the resources being used for Ukraine’s defense that he said would be better used to shore up Taiwan’s security against the growing threat from China. In his confirmation hearing to be part of the new Trump administration, however, he significantly softened his tone on the Chinese danger, when he said Taiwan is an important U.S. interest but “ not an existential one. “

Last week, given the widely recognized failure of Trump’s tragic Iran misadventure, Colby has again moved toward the more accommodationist approach to China favored by Trump. Speaking in the Philippines, America’s oldest security ally in Asia, Colby described the new approach to Chinese aggression as “ both realistic and perhaps bracing but also reassuring. ” He said the administration will now seek to accomplish its strategic objectives with China by downplaying areas of friction — Taiwan being the most dangerous among them.

“This means a strong and growing U.S. investment in the region,” he said. “But it is also coupled with a newfound but common sense expectation of much greater effort and contribution by our allies and partners. Not in a hectoring or unbalanced way. To the contrary, in a spirit of partnership, not dependency; of realism, not idle cloud-castle abstraction; of respect, not patronization.”

Colby listed America’s “counterparts in Manila, Bangkok, Jakarta, Singapore, Hanoi, Kuala Lumpur, and elsewhere — who have regular and frequent conversations with us. … They know that we are actively expanding our forward posture, accelerating the delivery of hard combat capabilities to the theater, and building out the physical architecture of a true denial defense.”

Colby’s list includes the capitals of two U.S. treaty allies and one former enemy, but no mention of Taipei. In fact, the name of Taiwan is absent from the entire presentation except for a passing reference to the first island chain as part of the National Security Strategy .

In these circumstances, Taiwan and its strong contingent of supporters in Congress and widely in the country are right to worry about what direction U.S. policy will take on this critical issue — and what unilateral concessions Trump might make on Taiwan’s fate.

Trump’s softer line on both South Korea and Taiwan suggest that his failed war in Iran, coming after his relatively easy and precise Venezuela operation, has disoriented his administration and distorted its perception of geostrategic realities. That does not bode well for international peace and stability.

Joseph Bosco served as China country director for the secretary of Defense from 2005 to 2006 and as Asia-Pacific director of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief from 2009 to 2010. He is a nonresident fellow at the Institute for Corean-American Studies, a member of the advisory board of the Global Taiwan Institute and member of the advisory board of the Vandenberg Coalition.

articles.title: Lutnick’s last-minute demands derailed Canada trade talks: Reports
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s interventions in the U.S.-Canada trade talks helped the weeks-long negotiations fall apart, according to multiple reports, thrusting the two countries into a trade war. U.S. and Canadian officials had felt good about an outline of a trade deal struck last Tuesday ahead of the original Wednesday deadline. President Trump took to…
articles.body:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s interventions in the U.S.-Canada trade talks helped the weeks-long negotiations fall apart, according to multiple reports, thrusting the two countries into a trade war .

U.S. and Canadian officials had felt good about an outline of a trade deal struck last Tuesday ahead of the original Wednesday deadline. President Trump took to social media to say that a deal had been struck, and he was pausing the 50 percent tariffs on some Canadian goods until Friday to finalize the paperwork.

But Lutnick was leery of Canadian proposals that would lower the tariff on autos to a level lower than what he wanted, according to The New York Times . He said instead that only a certain volume of aluminum should get lower tariff rates, and that heavy trucks should not have tariffs lowered like cars.

Canada produces some heavy trucks at the General Motors and Ford plants in Ontario.

Canadians put the blame on Lutnick for moving the goalposts at the eleventh hour, according to Bloomberg , while some business leaders were happy he was making demands on a deal they saw as hurting the U.S. metals industries.

When asked Saturday whether Lutnick’s involvement in the final days of negotiations was an impediment, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that’s “a question for the U.S. administration.”

Carney said his Canadian team was “unified … but you cannot say that about the United States administration.”

The talks between the U.S. and Canada fell apart on Friday, just hours before the tariffs were set to go into effect on items including wine, hockey sticks, cement and others.

Canada vowed to “match those tariffs dollar for dollar.” The tariffs apply to around $20 billion of Canadian goods.

Since then, Trump has threatened further hits on Canada — in the form of 50 percent tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and steel that would go into effect on New Year’s Day.

He accused Canada of “ripping off the United States of America for years” in a Truth Social post.

“On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with,” he wrote. “They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US! They do 95% of their business with the U.S., with us, the exact opposite!”

Canada said Monday it is expected to unveil retaliatory tariffs on the U.S. on Tuesday. They would go into effect on Sept. 8.

articles.title: Canada announces ‘dollar for dollar, rate for rate’ retaliatory tariffs on US
articles.summary: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on hundreds of American products as high as 50 percent Tuesday, just days after the collapse of negotiations between the two countries. Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said Canada will match the U.S.’s tariffs “dollar for dollar, rate for rate.” The tariffs would take effect Sept. 8. He said the 15…
articles.body:
Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on hundreds of American products as high as 50 percent Tuesday, just days after the collapse of negotiations between the two countries.

Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said Canada will match the U.S.’s tariffs “dollar for dollar, rate for rate.” The tariffs would take effect Sept. 8.

He said the 15 percent, 25 percent and 50 percent tariffs will be on $27.6 billion of imports from the U.S.

“For each product, our tariff will match the American tariff on the same type of Canadian good,” he said.

Arguably the biggest measure is Canada doubling its tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum to 50 percent to match the 50 percent the U.S. put on Canadian steel and aluminum.

“Those tariffs will have real consequences for Canadian workers, businesses, and communities across our nation,” Champagne said of the U.S. tariffs. “Canada must respond, and today we are in a proportionate, targeted, and strategic way.”

He said the countertariffs “are designed primarily to provide protection for Canadian industries impacted by the U.S. tariffs and allow them to compete against U.S. products in the Canadian market.”

Canada released a list of over 700 items that will be targeted with tariffs ranging from live fish, frozen fish, cheese, some apparel, carpets and metal products made of steel or aluminum, among others.

The U.S.’s 50 percent tariffs went into effect on Saturday across over $20 billion of Canadian imports after negotiations collapsed late Friday.

Trump threatened to impose 50 percent tariffs on a plethora of Canadian imports in response to “discriminatory” trade measures. The U.S. tariffs fall under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the administration said when announcing them last month.

Section 338 is a long-dormant law that allows the president to impose tariffs of up to 50 percent on a country found to discriminate against U.S. products. It does not require an investigation before tariffs are imposed.

Trump on Monday then threatened to hit Canada with 50 percent tariffs on imported cars, trucks, auto parts and steel, which would take effect on New Year’s Day.

“Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” he wrote on Truth Social. “Their ridiculously high tariffs on our Farmers and farm products has made life impossible for these great American Patriots, and has long created a 60 Billion Dollar Deficit between our two Countries. Not sustainable, and NOT ANYMORE!”

Trump said Canada will no longer “be treated like a State.”

“On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with,” he said. “They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US! They do 95% of their business with the U.S., with us, the exact opposite!”

Canada for its part has remained strong against the U.S. measures. Canadian officials also announced a $7.5 billion CAD package to help support domestic businesses that are harmed by the tariffs.

articles.title: Doug Ford responds to Trump’s Lake Ontario taunt: ‘A lot of rhetoric’
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed President Trump’s Tuesday threat to rename a Canadian lake in honor of the U.S., a day after the pair publicly exchanged insults amid an escalating trade fight between the two countries. “I think it’s a lot of rhetoric,” Ford told CNN’s Wolf Blitzer, noting Canada’s role as a “number one…
articles.body:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed President Trump’s Tuesday threat to rename a Canadian lake in honor of the U.S., a day after the pair publicly exchanged insults amid an escalating trade fight between the two countries.

“I think it’s a lot of rhetoric,” Ford told CNN’s Wolf Blitzer, noting Canada’s role as a “number one customer” for more than a dozen U.S. states.

“We’re strong believers in being a sovereign country, and when President Trump wants to attack our sovereignty and attack our businesses and people in Ontario, I can’t roll over,” he said. “My job is to protect Ontario and Canada, and ironically, protecting the American people.”

The president wrote in a Truth Social post on Tuesday morning that his administration was “giving serious consideration” to renaming Lake Ontario to “Lake America” amid the trade war between the U.S. and Canada.

Trump added that he did not “expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer.”

The post followed Trump’s earlier move to impose 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods.

Ford lashed out at these levies on Monday, reiterating his threat to cut the province’s power exports to U.S. states. Ontario’s power grid directly connects to Michigan, New York and Minnesota.

“We power 1.5 million homes and businesses. Everything’s on the table. I’ll do whatever it takes,” the Canadian official told reporters.

Ford called on both sides of the fight to bring down the temperature on Tuesday, acknowledging in his interview with CNN that “things got a little heated” between him and the president.

“Let’s negotiate a fair deal because it’s hurting the U.S. It’s hurting Canada, and we just want to make sure that we have a fair deal,” he said.

Canada announced Tuesday retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on a wide range of U.S. goods that will go into effect on Sept. 8. This came after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s statement last week that the country would match the U.S. tariffs “dollar for dollar.”

Ford told CNN that the U.S. tariffs ultimately harm Americans.

“I do not understand why he wants to attack Canada nonstop,” he said. “We’re the closest friends and allies, and make no mistake about it, Canadians still love the American people. They love the U.S.”

“Let’s negotiate a fair deal because it’s hurting the U.S. It’s hurting Canada, and we just want to make sure that we have a fair deal,” he said.

Canada announced Tuesday retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on a wide range of U.S. goods that will go into effect on Sept. 8. This came after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s statement last week that the country would match the U.S. tariffs “dollar for dollar.”
Ford told CNN that the U.S. tariffs ultimately harm Americans.

“I do not understand why he wants to attack Canada nonstop,” he said. “We’re the closest friends and allies, and make no mistake about it, Canadians still love the American people. They love the U.S.”

articles.title: Penny Doe identified 36 years after remains found in Pennsylvania | Dateline
articles.summary: The remains were found in July 1990 in Monroe Township in Clarion County. Investigators are working to figure out what happened that summer.
articles.body: In July 1990, an unidentified woman was found in Clarion County, Pennsylvania. There was a penny in each of the woman’s jeans pockets, a small detail that would earn the woman a nickname: “Penny Doe.” For the past 36 years, her identity has remained unknown. Now, she has her name back. On Monday, Clarion County District Attorney Drew Welsh held a news conference to share the news. “Today is an important and significant day in the investigation into the death of Penny Doe,” he said. “Through the dedicated work of investigators over the past 36 years, today, I am able to reveal the identity of Penny Doe.” The DA outlined the steps taken over the last three decades of investigation. He described it as a “true team effort,” but cautioned that since the investigation is ongoing, some information would not be shared to protect the integrity of the case. “On July 22, 1990, a woman’s body was discovered in Monroe Township, Clarion County, by four local children,” Welsh recapped. “Three of those local children are here with us today.” In 2022, Dateline featured Penny Doe’s case in its “Cold Case Spotlight” digital series. We spoke with Angie Clinger, one of the children who found Penny Doe’s remains in a tunnel underneath a railroad trestle. “We freaked out,” she told Dateline in 2022. “I don’t think I ever ran so quick in my life.” The children reported their finding to the authorities, and the investigation began. The autopsy determined the unknown woman died as a result of “blunt trauma to the right side of her head,” Welsh said. “From that point forward, the death has been considered a homicide, and has remained open.” For the past 36 years, investigators have worked with two goals in mind. “The first was to identify who Penny Doe was, and the second was to prove what had happened to her and bring those responsible to justice.” Authorities have used various methods to try to identify her: fingerprint identification, checking her DNA against known missing persons, and testing her remains by analyzing her bones and teeth. “The Pennsylvania State Police have investigated and ruled out over 100 individuals of being Penny Doe,” Welsh stated. “There have been re-creations made of her face, and artists renderings of what she might have looked like.” A clay representation, illustrations and computer-generated images have also been made. And while those brought in leads and tips that were followed up on, they ultimately did not bring investigators any closer to finding her identity. Welsh said that from 1990 through 2020, when he began reviewing the case files, “there had been constant work done” by the Pennsylvania State Police. “After seeing all the hard work that came before me, I wanted to make sure that we got the case moving forward,” he said. They again looked into testing the DNA as technology continued to evolve. In 2023, police identified a funding source via a federal grant called the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant. In March 2024, they partnered with Othram Labs for a DNA extraction. A family tree was developed, and a potential sister identified. Police contacted the woman, who submitted her DNA, and the DNA came back as a match. “Ladies and gentlemen, Penny Doe has a name,” Welsh announced on Monday. “Penny Doe is Windy Buchanan.” She was born in October 1970 in Kentucky. Windy and her siblings did not have an easy upbringing, Welsh shared at the news conference. “The last time her family saw Windy, was that she and her family and two brothers pulled off on a random off-ramp looking for a place to rest and eat,” he said. “Windy’s last words to her family were, ‘Bye, Dad, I’m leaving.’” They never saw her again. Welsh would not share any additional information about where exactly that highway off-ramp was located. It is unclear where the off-ramp was in relation to the tunnel where the remains were found. Welsh said Windy’s family had searched for her over the years but were unsuccessful. Her younger sister, Tania Buchanan Boyd, spoke at the news conference, and shared more about who Windy was as a person. “My sister was fierce and she was kind, and she was loving,” she said. “She was the firstborn of five, and she would often watch over us.” “She was basically always there for me,” Tania said. “She was creative and artistic. She loved horses and animals. She was convinced that horseshoes brought good luck.” They weren’t the only things Windy believed brought good luck. “She always thought that finding a penny heads up brought you good luck,” Tania said. “Find a penny, pick it up. And all the day, you have good luck.” Tania also thanked the investigators who worked the case for more than three decades. “Our family deeply, deeply appreciates each and every one of you for staying with the case,” she said. “For many years we did search for Windy. We prayed that she would somehow be found, or that she might return to us one day.” “One of our deepest and longest-held prayers has finally been answered,” Tania said. “But it’s not over. We know where she was at, but we don’t know what happened to her.” “It’s important that our first goal has been accomplished,” Welsh stated. “My sincerest hope today is that this will start a new beginning to this investigation, where we will be able to answer that second question — that second goal — to find out who did this and bring them to justice.” Welsh urges anyone who knows anything about what happened to Windy Buchanan to please come forward. “It was easy for you to stay silent when it was an anonymous Penny Doe. Those days are done,” he said. “Now, you must speak.” “It’s never too late to come forward,” sister Tania said. “Windy deserves the truth, and our family deserves all of the answers.” If you have any information that could help the investigation, please contact the Pennsylvania State Police at 814-226-1710. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Pakistan, Iran made ‘significant progress’ to end US-Iran war, minister says
articles.summary: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday announced that “significant progress” has been made toward ending the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran, according to Pakistan’s interior minister, Reuters reported. Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s army chief, met with Iranian officials in Tehran about measures to prevent the conflict from growing and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which…
articles.body:
Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday announced that “significant progress” has been made toward ending the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran, according to Pakistan’s interior minister, Reuters reported .

Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s army chief, met with Iranian officials in Tehran about measures to prevent the conflict from growing and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been closed under Iranian control, causing gas prices to skyrocket.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who traveled with Munir, said their meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was “very positive and productive.”

“The Iranian President candidly shared his Government’s perspective and concerns, and we had a very constructive exchange on the issues involved,” Naqvi wrote on the social platform X . “Significant progress was made, and the meeting concluded on a highly positive note. We remain hopeful that this momentum will help pave the way for further progress and lasting peace in the region.”

Naqvi said the discussion focused on the conflict and a path forward for the region. He added that they talked about the steps needed to restore the interim peace deal signed by the U.S. and Iran in June, which expired last week.

Munir called President Trump ahead of the talks in Tehran, Reuters reported.

The Pakistani delegation’s visit comes as Iran and Oman announced a plan to allow navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and clear mines placed in the waterway. Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran about a “phased framework” for the strait.

“The proposed framework includes the establishment of a joint temporary navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines,” Oman’s Foreign Ministry posted on the social platform X .

Talks regarding the strait’s future would include an agreement on “a mechanism for information-sharing, traffic management, and the provision of relevant navigational and security services.”

“In this context, both sides underscored the importance of convening joint discussions with regional states bordering the waters of the Gulf,” the foreign minister’s office added. “They further stressed the need to uphold applicable international law and respect the sovereign rights of the coastal states.”

Trump previously threatened Oman over potentially striking a deal with Iran, warning the country that “we’ll bomb the s— out of them” if it “gets in the way.”

Iranian officials have insisted that the strait will reopen after Trump withdraws a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports, pays compensation for damages from the war, lifts sanctions and unfreezes assets.

The Trump administration has also warned other countries that they could face economic consequences if they do not cut off their financial ties to the Iranian regime. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced “ Operation Economic Outcast ,” a new campaign to constrict Iran’s economy, but offered few specific details.

“Well, we are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior, why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” Bessent said in response to a reporter’s question about the operation’s details.

articles.title: Secret Service says it’s aware of Iranian video threatening Barron Trump
articles.summary: The Secret Service on Tuesday said it was aware of a video threatening President Trump’s son, Barron, being circulated by Iranian state media. Clips suggest that Iran’s leaders are tracking Barron’s whereabouts and offering a $10 million reward to those who can provide insight into his location, according to reports from ABC News. “The U.S.…
articles.body:
The Secret Service on Tuesday said it was aware of a video threatening President Trump’s son, Barron, being circulated by Iranian state media.

Clips suggest that Iran’s leaders are tracking Barron’s whereabouts and offering a $10 million reward to those who can provide insight into his location, according to reports from ABC News .

“The U.S. Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees,” Secret Service spokesperson Nate Herring said in a statement to NewsNation, The Hill’s sister network.

“Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence,” Herring added.

In previous instances, Iran has circulated videos and statements threatening to kill the president and his family members. The stakes have heightened as the war in Iran nears the six-month mark with no clear end in sight.

The Trump administration has waged both military and economic war on Tehran and pushed its leaders to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial traffic.

Iran has refused but agreed to work with Oman to open two pathways through the critical waterway for a fee.

Since the U.S. and Israel first struck Iran in February, its leaders have been seeking revenge for the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the strikes.

Iran held a weeklong national ceremony in July to commemorate Khamenei’s life while appointing his son, Mojtaba Khamenei, to serve in his place.

Mojtaba Khamenei was reportedly injured in U.S.-Israeli strikes and has remained absent from direct negotiations with U.S. envoys.

The U.S. and Iran reached a brief ceasefire on June 17 following Pakistan-mediated talks.

President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian signed a memorandum of understanding enshrining a 14-point agreement that halted military operations and aimed to reopen the strait.

However, the fragile ceasefire began to break down in early July after renewed vessel attacks in the strait, and the 60-day agreement ultimately expired last week.

articles.title: Democrats push Rubio on Board of Peace ‘slush fund’ for Trump
articles.summary: House Democrats are applying new scrutiny on President Trump’s Board of Peace, demanding answers on how his inner circle is using American tax dollars for a “slush fund” and planning to profit off plans to rebuild the Gaza Strip. The Trump administration was forced to halt the transfer of $50 million to the board in…
articles.body:
House Democrats are applying new scrutiny on President Trump’s Board of Peace, demanding answers on how his inner circle is using American tax dollars for a “slush fund” and planning to profit off plans to rebuild the Gaza Strip.

The Trump administration was forced to halt the transfer of $50 million to the board in July, in the face of pushback from lawmakers who said the State Department could not answer basic questions about the board’s structure, oversight of the funds, and whether Trump could use the funds to compensate himself.

Those questions form the basis of a letter sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday and obtained exclusively by The Hill. The letter also signals that Democrats will open an investigation into Trump’s Board of Peace if they take the majority in the House after the November midterm elections, in which case they would gain subpoena power.

Reps. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) and Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), the ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs committees, respectively, call for Rubio to answer basic questions about the board’s structure, funding and oversight, nine months after its creation.

“The fact that the Trump Administration, with your help, is attempting to transfer taxpayer dollars to the Board of Peace, an opaque organization primed for corruption, raises serious concerns that public funds could be once again misused by the President and his family and friends,” the lawmakers wrote.

Trump created the Board of Peace in October as part of a plan to end the devastating war between Israel and Hamas in the Gaza Strip, appointing himself as “chairman for life” with apparent unilateral control over the board’s decisions and how money is spent on reconstruction — even beyond his presidency.

The United Nations Security Council endorsed the board until 2027. But in January, Trump expanded the board’s mission to tackle conflict around the world, setting it up to outlive the Security Council deadline. The president solicited billion-dollar pledges from countries in exchange for lifetime membership and promised an initial pledge of $10 billion from the U.S. government.

A Board of Peace official earlier told The Hill that hundreds of millions of dollars have been collected to finance the Gaza peace plan. The Financial Times reported in May that donors preferred placing funds in a bank account managed by J.P. Morgan , rather than the account set up at the World Bank.

Democrats and other critics say there are no clear answers on who is auditing and conducting oversight of the J.P. Morgan account.

On July 29, the State Department notified Congress it was rescinding $50 million in funding it was sending to the Board of Peace from its budget for international organizations and programs.

The notification followed intense pressure from Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, a congressional aide told The Hill. The Board of Peace did not respond to a letter Shaheen sent them in June raising questions about funds, but it has started briefing committee staff, the congressional aide said.

Raskin and Meeks’s letter adds to that pressure. The lawmakers argue that basic questions on whether the Board of Peace is a public or private entity, a U.S. organization or international, or “even a false entity altogether” are unanswered.

“Can anyone assure Congress that billions of dollars from U.S. taxpayers and foreign governments will not be flowing into the pockets of President Trump, members of his family, corrupt and incompetent contractors or business partners, or political allies and foot soldiers of the President?” the lawmakers wrote.

Raskin and Meeks also argue that Trump’s executive order establishing the Board of Peace as a “public international organization” — which would protect it from lawsuits and certain searches from federal law enforcement — is without merit.

A Board of Peace official earlier told The Hill that the board “is an international organization established under international law. Its legal status and mandate derive from the foundational arrangements establishing it and the consent of its participating members.”

But Raskin and Meeks said that such an organization must be established under a treaty or an act of Congress.

“The Board of Peace was created out of thin air and whole cloth by the President, without any input from Congress about any aspect of its operation,” they wrote.

The lawmakers argue that Board of Peace members have been “explicit” about their intention to use it for “private profit-making purposes,” pointing to statements by Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law and a board member, advertising “amazing investment opportunities” when promoting the administration’s Gaza plan to the World Economic Forum in Davos in January.

And Raskin further points out that the administration’s goal to trademark Board of Peace earlier this year served as a flashing red light for “backroom deals and procedural illegitimacy.”

Earlier this year, in a move that Raskin described as “almost certainly illegal,” the director of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, John Squires, applied for trademarks on behalf of the board. Squires told Raskin at a Judiciary hearing in March that he filed the trademark to preserve access to the Board of Peace website address in his authority as adviser to the president.

“After Judiciary Committee Democrats demanded information on this trademark application in three oversight letters to Director Squires, he abruptly abandoned the applications but failed to respond to any of our letters or provide information as to who directed him to apply for this trademark for the Board in the first place,” Raskin and Meeks wrote.

The lawmakers gave Rubio a Sept. 8 deadline to answer more than a dozen questions on who manages the Board of Peace, the decisionmaking process, who has the authority to make financial decisions, staffing, what bank accounts are being used and how it’s being overseen, among other questions.

“We will work with you to guarantee the American people full transparency about how their tax dollars are being funneled to — and spent by — this organization never established or authorized by Congress but now poised to receive substantial public funding from the State Department under your direction,” they wrote.

There’s been little progress in finally ending the conflict between Israel and Hamas in Gaza, the narrow seaside territory divided under majority Israeli control but with nearly 2 million Palestinians living under Hamas control. Thousands are displaced, living in bare-bones temporary shelters of tarps or damaged buildings and facing shortages of water, food and medicine.

Last month, the Board of Peace proposed a roadmap to disarm Hamas, and it is pushing Israel to accept the proposal. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has shown little interest in finding common ground with Hamas as he fights for his political survival in upcoming elections.

The board is working toward developing a “pilot zone” where tens of thousands of Palestinians could move into reconstructed neighborhoods in southern Gaza free of Hamas control.

A Board of Peace official earlier told The Hill that the board “is an international organization established under international law. Its legal status and mandate derive from the foundational arrangements establishing it and the consent of its participating members.”
But Raskin and Meeks said that such an organization must be established under a treaty or an act of Congress.
“The Board of Peace was created out of thin air and whole cloth by the President, without any input from Congress about any aspect of its operation,” they wrote.

The lawmakers argue that Board of Peace members have been “explicit” about their intention to use it for “private profit-making purposes,” pointing to statements by Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law and a board member, advertising “amazing investment opportunities” when promoting the administration’s Gaza plan to the World Economic Forum in Davos in January.
And Raskin further points out that the administration’s goal to trademark Board of Peace earlier this year served as a flashing red light for “backroom deals and procedural illegitimacy.”

Earlier this year, in a move that Raskin described as “almost certainly illegal,” the director of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, John Squires, applied for trademarks on behalf of the board. Squires told Raskin at a Judiciary hearing in March that he filed the trademark to preserve access to the Board of Peace website address in his authority as adviser to the president.

“After Judiciary Committee Democrats demanded information on this trademark application in three oversight letters to Director Squires, he abruptly abandoned the applications but failed to respond to any of our letters or provide information as to who directed him to apply for this trademark for the Board in the first place,” Raskin and Meeks wrote.

The lawmakers gave Rubio a Sept. 8 deadline to answer more than a dozen questions on who manages the Board of Peace, the decisionmaking process, who has the authority to make financial decisions, staffing, what bank accounts are being used and how it’s being overseen, among other questions.

“We will work with you to guarantee the American people full transparency about how their tax dollars are being funneled to — and spent by — this organization never established or authorized by Congress but now poised to receive substantial public funding from the State Department under your direction,” they wrote.

There’s been little progress in finally ending the conflict between Israel and Hamas in Gaza, the narrow seaside territory divided under majority Israeli control but with nearly 2 million Palestinians living under Hamas control. Thousands are displaced, living in bare-bones temporary shelters of tarps or damaged buildings and facing shortages of water, food and medicine.

Last month, the Board of Peace proposed a roadmap to disarm Hamas, and it is pushing Israel to accept the proposal. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has shown little interest in finding common ground with Hamas as he fights for his political survival in upcoming elections.
The board is working toward developing a “pilot zone” where tens of thousands of Palestinians could move into reconstructed neighborhoods in southern Gaza free of Hamas control.

articles.title: Canada’s minister of industry: ‘We’ll always call it Lake Ontario’
articles.summary: Mélanie Joly, Canada’s minister of industry, rebuffed President Trump’s warning to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America” on Tuesday, saying Canadians will “always call it Lake Ontario.” “We’re proud of our Great Lakes,” Joly told reporters during a Tuesday press conference. “We’ve navigated the St. Lawrence River, the Great Lakes, for thousands of years, and it…
articles.body:
Mélanie Joly, Canada’s minister of industry, rebuffed President Trump’s warning to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America” on Tuesday, saying Canadians will “always call it Lake Ontario.”

“We’re proud of our Great Lakes,” Joly told reporters during a Tuesday press conference. “We’ve navigated the St. Lawrence River, the Great Lakes, for thousands of years, and it was part of a foundation of our country. And we’ll just stand up for what we have.”

Met with applause, Joly added that while “all these shenanigans are happening” — referring to the president’s ongoing trade war with Canada — “we’ll just be smart and we’ll be strategic and we’ll fight back.”

Trump’s warning resembles his 2025 executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico to the “ Gulf of America ” — a move he described at the time as retaliation against the U.S.’s southern neighbor for “allowing millions of people to pour into our country.”

On Instagram, the official White House account shared a photo of a U.S. map appearing as though it was built using Legos. Above the Great Lakes region appears a rectangle containing the words “Lake America,” while the southern gulf has a similar sign that reads “Gulf of America.”

The renewed trade war between Washington and Ottawa began after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney removed negotiators from trade talks with the U.S. over the weekend, causing a new set of tariffs on several Canadian goods to go into effect.

Carney then announced that, starting Sept. 8, Ottawa would enact retaliatory tariffs in response to the U.S.’s 50 percent tariffs . He told reporters that it would “match Washington’s new tariffs dollar for dollar in order to protect Canadian workers, farmers, families and businesses.”

François-Philippe Champagne, Canada’s minister of finance, said Tuesday that Canada will impose 15 percent, 25 percent and 50 percent tariffs on $27.6 billion of U.S. goods. Canada is doubling its tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum to 50 percent — exactly matching the U.S.’s rate.

“For each product, our tariff will match the American tariff on the same type of Canadian good,” Champagne said.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford preceded Joly in clapping back at Trump’s warning, telling CNN on Tuesday that the threats were a “lot of rhetoric.”

“We’re strong believers in being a sovereign country, and when President Trump wants to attack our sovereignty and attack our businesses and people in Ontario, I can’t roll over,” he told the network’s Wolf Blitzer. “My job is to protect Ontario and Canada, and ironically, protecting the American people.”

The Ontario premier called on both sides of the fight to bring down the temperature, telling Blitzer that “things got a little heated” between him and Trump.

“Let’s negotiate a fair deal because it’s hurting the U.S. It’s hurting Canada, and we just want to make sure that we have a fair deal,” Ford said.

articles.title: Hillary Clinton says Republicans ‘secretly cheering’ for Mark Carney amid US-Canada trade negotiation
articles.summary: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton claimed that Republicans are “secretly cheering” for Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney amid tension between Washington and Ottawa over trade. “I can’t imagine that even in the Republican cloakroom in the Senate, there’s much enthusiasm for going into a trade war with Canada,” Clinton said Monday night during an…
articles.body:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton claimed that Republicans are “secretly cheering” for Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney amid tension between Washington and Ottawa over trade.

“I can’t imagine that even in the Republican cloakroom in the Senate, there’s much enthusiasm for going into a trade war with Canada,” Clinton said Monday night during an event in New York.

She added that 40 percent of Ohio’s exports and 60 percent of Michigan’s exports go to Canada.

“I can’t imagine that the Republicans in those states, or literally anywhere in the country, are enthusiastic about this nonsense that [President] Trump is promoting, and probably secretly cheering Mark Carney for standing up to him and doing what he’s now doing on behalf of his country,” Clinton said.

Canada unveiled retaliatory tariffs Tuesday on the U.S. in the wake of President Trump’s fresh threats to heat up the trade war between the two countries.

Carney said Canada would match American tariffs “dollar for dollar” following 50 percent tariffs the Trump administration placed on more than $20 billion in Canadian goods that went into effect over the weekend. Ottawa’s retaliatory levies are set to go into effect Sept. 8.

The prime minister said Monday that Canada may have to use more precise retaliation to protect its workers and businesses as Trump threatens new 50 percent tariffs aimed at cars, trucks, auto parts and steel going into effect at the beginning of next year.

Throughout Trump’s second term, U.S.-Canada relations have been shakier than usual, with trade disputes erupting between the two countries and Trump talking about acquiring the U.S.’s northern neighbor as the 51st state.

When reached for comment, White House spokesperson Kush Desai said in an emailed statement that “if Hillary Clinton knew anything about Ohio or Michigan – or Wisconsin and Pennsylvania, for that matter – she wouldn’t have so humiliatingly lost to President Trump in 2016.”

articles.title: Auditor-fiscal tentou jogar celular no sanitário durante prisão no CE | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois empresários também foram presos, na Bahia, durante a operação realizada nesta terça-feira (25) contra o grupo, acusado de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e fraudes em importações.
articles.summary: Dois empresários também foram presos, na Bahia, durante a operação realizada nesta terça (25) contra o grupo, acusado de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e fraudes em importações.
articles.body:
O auditor-fiscal Francisco Eliezer Viana da Silva , suspeito de receber R$ 6,8 milhões em propina de um esquema para fraudar importações no Aeroporto de Fortaleza , teria tentado jogar o próprio celular no vaso sanitário ao perceber a chegada dos agentes da Polícia Federal que realizaram sua prisão nesta terça-feira (25). A informação foi repassada ao g1 por uma fonte relacionada às investigações.

Além de Eliezer, dois empresários foram presos na Bahia: Rodolfo Sergio Martins Maia e Hugo Andrade Mendonça Santos. As capturas ocorreram na Operação Snooker 2 , que também cumpriu 15 de busca e apreensão, além de apreensão de bens como carros e relógios de luxo. As ações ocorreram nas cidades de Fortaleza , Caucaia e Eusébio, no Ceará; e em Salvador, na Bahia.

Segundo apuração do g1 , a equipe enviada para cumprir o mandado de prisão contra Eliezier precisou arrombar o apartamento do servidor porque ele não atendeu ao chamado para abrir a porta. Quando a equipe entrou no imóvel, descobriu que ele teria jogado o aparelho celular na caixa de água do vaso sanitário. O equipamento foi recuperado, mas ainda não se sabe se será possível restaurar os arquivos.

Francisco Eliezer é servidor concursado da Receita Federal desde 1994. Ele estava no cargo no Aeroporto de Fortaleza desde dezembro de 2016 e tinha um salário mensal de mais de R$ 30 mil. Em junho de 2026, quando já era investigado, ele chegou a receber R$ 44 mil devido a gratificação natalina.

O auditor-fiscal atuava no gabinete da inspetoria do aeroporto e é suspeito de interferir irregularmente em despachos aduaneiros e fornecer informações e orientações sigilosas sobre comércio exterior. Em troca, ele recebia vantagens como a propina. Ele é apontado como chefe da organização criminosa, com atuação desde pelo menos 2020.

Segundo a investigação, o grupo importava itens caros, como prata e eletrônicos, e os declarava como itens de menor valor com o objetivo de burlar a fiscalização aduaneira, pagar menos impostos e lucrar mais. Para isso, eles contavam com a atuação direta de Francisco Eliezer no fornecimento de informações, obtenção de laudos periciais falsos e até mesmo interferência direta na fiscalização.

Entenda como era o esquema de fraude em importação com propina milionária

As investigações identificaram movimentações superiores a R$ 27 milhões entre empresas ligadas ao esquema, de acordo com a Receita Federal. O grupo também teria adquirido aproximadamente R$ 31,8 milhões em criptoativos, sem compatibilidade com as receitas formalmente declaradas.

PF faz operação contra fraudes em importações no Aeroporto de Fortaleza — Foto: PF/Divulgação

Os alvos da operação poderão responder pelos crimes de organização criminosa, corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e fraudes em operações de importação. Até o momento, o grupo já teve mais de R$ 26 milhões bloqueados em contas bancárias de empresas e pessoas físicas envolvidas nas atividades criminosas, além da apreensão de veículos importados e de uma embarcação de luxo.

Ao g1 , o advogado de defesa de Francisco Eliezer, Marcelo Oliveira , afirmou ter recebido com surpresa a decisão pela prisão do auditor-fiscal, uma vez que ele já havia sido alvo de um mandado de busca e apreensão anteriormente e havia sido denunciado formalmente pelo Ministério Público, e nenhum fato novo teria ocorrido desde então.

O advogado afirmou que, nesse momento, está tomando "todas as medidas jurídicas necessárias para reverter a prisão decretada, para além da demonstração da sua inocência, junto à ação penal".

A reportagem não conseguiu localizar as defesas dos empresários Rodolfo Sergio Martins Maia e Hugo Andrade Mendonça Santos.

Segundo as investigações, o grupo era hierarquizado e dividido em quatro núcleos: público, empresarial, financeiro e auxiliar. As tarefas eram divididas entre um agente público, empresários do setor de importação e pessoas responsáveis por movimentar e ocultar os recursos ilícitos.

No centro do esquema estaria o auditor-fiscal Francisco Eliezer, da Receita Federal. Ele teria fornecido informações e orientações sigilosas sobre comércio exterior em benefício de empresas importadoras e despachantes aduaneiros.

Umas delas envolve uma empresa importadora, administrada por um empresário cearense, que importava joias de prata e declarava os produtos como semijoias ou bijuterias de metal comum, de valor tributário muito inferior. Conforme a denúncia, o empresário recebia apoio de Eliezer para obter laudos periciais fraudados que atestavam falsamente a natureza do material.

A segunda frente envolve um casal de empresários de nacionalidade chinesa, também à frente de outra importadora. O casal subfaturava produtos eletrônicos para reduzir o pagamento de tributos , contando com a intercessão direta de Eliezer para driblar a fiscalização aduaneira . A propina paga por esse grupo é estimada em pelo menos R$ 2,5 milhões.

Primeira fase da operação Snooke, realizada em 2025, apreendeu dinheiro com os suspeitos — Foto: Polícia Federal/ Divulgação

Ainda segundo o MPF, outro grupo de investigados é apontado como o núcleo financeiro da organização . Nesse grupo estaria um contador responsável pela constituição de diversas empresas de fachada em nome de terceiros. Ele estaria encarregado de movimentar os valores ilícitos e disfarçar o repasse de propina ao agente público.

"Dois integrantes desse núcleo, responsáveis de fato por empresas importadoras de fachada, teriam pago ao auditor-fiscal, em contrapartida a informações privilegiadas sobre procedimentos internos da Receita Federal, pelo menos R$ 3,1 milhões", explica o órgão.

A denúncia ainda fala de um suposto núcleo auxiliar do esquema, formado por familiares de Francisco Eliezer (entre eles cônjuge, filhas, irmãos e um cunhado) , que teriam recebido pagamentos e bens adquiridos com recursos de origem ilícita. Nesse núcleo, também estariam pessoas que emprestaram seus nomes para figurar formalmente como responsáveis por empresas e contas bancárias usadas na lavagem de dinheiro.

O núcleo financeiro é apontado, em conjunto com um núcleo auxiliar, como responsável pela movimentação de mais de R$ 103,3 milhões por meio de empresas sem atividade econômica real.

Polícia Federal apreende em Salvador (BA) lancha de grupo suspeito de fraudar importações em Fortaleza (CE) — Foto: Polícia Federal

articles.title: Incêndio em hospital no Paquistão deixa ao menos 15 bebês mortos, diz TV local | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo foi desencadeado por uma falha nos sistemas de ar-condicionado. Havia 16 recém-nascidos na ala de ginecologia do hospital quando o incêndio começou, um dos quais foi resgatado.
articles.summary: Fogo foi desencadeado por uma falha nos sistemas de ar-condicionado. Havia 16 recém-nascidos na ala de ginecologia do hospital quando o incêndio começou, um dos quais foi resgatado.
articles.body:
Ao menos 15 bebês morreram em um incêndio em um hospital em Islamabad, capital do Paquistão, nesta quarta-feira (26). De acordo com a Geo TV, emissora local, o fogo foi desencadeado por uma falha nos sistemas de ar-condicionado.

O incêndio, que começou no hospital do Instituto de Ciências Médicas do Paquistão (PIMS), começou por volta das 7 horas (23h de terça, no horário de Brasília), disse a emissora, acrescentando que "operações de resfriamento" estavam em andamento.

Havia 16 recém-nascidos na ala de ginecologia do hospital quando o incêndio começou, um dos quais foi resgatado, segundo Geo.

articles.summary: Decisão unânime foi tomada nesta terça-feira (25). Imóvel seria destinado a projeto de centro de inteligência artificial e teve desapropriação questionada pelo Ministério Público.
articles.body:
O Tribunal de Justiça do Rio de Janeiro (TJ-RJ) manteve, por unanimidade, a suspensão do leilão do imóvel do Grupo Sendas localizado na Rua Barão de Itambi, nº 50, em Botafogo, na Zona Sul do Rio. A decisão foi tomada nesta terça-feira (25), por 3 votos a 0, e impede a realização do leilão enquanto a Justiça não julgar o mérito da disputa sobre a desapropriação.

📱Baixe o app do g1 para ver notícias do RJ em tempo real e de graça

O imóvel foi desapropriado pela Prefeitura do Rio para viabilizar a implantação de um centro de tecnologia, inovação e ensino, com projeto voltado à pesquisa em inteligência artificial. O edital previa lance mínimo de R$ 36 milhões .

A decisão ocorre pouco mais de um mês depois de um parecer do Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ) que defendeu o prosseguimento da ação popular que questiona o decreto municipal. No documento, o procurador de Justiça Marlon Oberst Cordovil apontou elementos que, segundo ele, indicam possível desvio de finalidade na desapropriação.

Prefeitura desapropria prédio com comércio ativo em Botafogo; vereador e moradores apontam ilegalidade — Foto: Reprodução Google Maps

O leilão havia sido suspenso anteriormente por decisão liminar da Justiça após recurso apresentado pelo Grupo Sendas, proprietário do imóvel. A empresa contesta a desapropriação e sustenta que o prédio não se enquadraria nos critérios para aplicação do instrumento da hasta pública.

Nesta terça, o tribunal analisou o recurso e decidiu manter a suspensão. Com isso, o leilão previsto pela Prefeitura do Rio não poderá ser realizado enquanto a suspensão estiver em vigor.

Entenda a desapropriação de prédio em Botafogo que virou disputa entre prefeitura, moradores e empresários

Leilão de prédio em Botafogo: Edital exige centro de IA

Sendas diz que decisão reforça questionamentos

O Grupo Sendas afirma que o imóvel não estava e não está abandonado nem subutilizado . Segundo a empresa, o prédio abriga uma academia em funcionamento, enquanto o espaço térreo passa por reformas para receber um novo supermercado, cujo contrato de locação já foi firmado.

Para Arthur Sendas Filho, presidente do Grupo Sendas, a decisão do tribunal representa um avanço na disputa judicial.

“A decisão de hoje preserva o imóvel até que a Justiça confirme definitivamente a ilegalidade do decreto de desapropriação. O parecer do Ministério Público trouxe elementos importantes ao processo e reforça a necessidade de que o poder público observe os requisitos legais e a finalidade pública ao promover uma desapropriação”, afirma.

O grupo afirma que espera que a Prefeitura do Rio encerre a disputa para permitir a abertura definitiva do Supermercado Mundial, que tem contrato assinado para ocupar a loja.

articles.title: DetranRS passa a pedir exame toxicológico para categorias A e B da CNH | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida entra em vigor em 1º de setembro e afeta candidatos que buscam a primeira habilitação para carro e moto. Exame deve ser feito em laboratório credenciado.
articles.summary: Medida entra em vigor em 1º de setembro e afeta candidatos que buscam a primeira habilitação para carro e moto. Exame deve ser feito em laboratório credenciado
articles.body:
O Departamento Estadual de Trânsito do Rio Grande do Sul (DetranRS) vai passar a exigir que os candidatos à primeira habilitação façam exame toxicológico . A medida entra em vigor em 1º de setembro .

Em dezembro do ano passado, o Congresso Nacional aprovou a exigência do exame para a primeira via da Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) nas categorias A e B . Desta forma, quem pretende tirar a habilitação precisa apresentar resultado negativo em um teste que identifica o uso de drogas nos últimos meses.

A exigência, prevista no Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB), vale para quem iniciar formalmente o processo de habilitação no RS a partir do próximo mês.

Já exigido para categorias profissionais (C, D e E), em exames periódicos, o teste toxicológico passa a valer também para a primeira habilitação de carro e moto , tendo como base legal a Lei 15.153, de 2025, que incluiu os parágrafos 10 e 11 ao art. 148-A do CTB.

O exame deve ser realizado em laboratório credenciado na Secretaria Nacional de Trânsito (Senatran), podendo ser feito em qualquer etapa do processo de habilitação. A relação de laboratórios credenciados está disponível no site da Senatran.

A expedição da Permissão para Dirigir somente ocorrerá após o laboratório registrar no sistema o resultado negativo do exame toxicológico do candidato.

O exame toxicológico usa amostras de cabelo , pelos ou unhas e identifica o consumo de substâncias psicoativas em um período retrospectivo mínimo de 90 dias , podendo chegar a 180 dias.

O processo envolve coleta em postos credenciados, análise laboratorial e emissão de laudo rastreável. A confiabilidade é garantida por normas técnicas, cadeia de custódia e procedimentos que evitam contaminação ou adulteração da amostra.

articles.title: As duas frentes da guerra comercial de Trump - O Assunto #1791 | G1
articles.standfirst: Casa Branca anuncia 'Dia D' contra Irã e impõe sanções contra pessoas e organizações ligadas ao regime. E o Canadá irá realizar um tarifaço em retaliação às tarifas americanas.
articles.summary: Casa Branca anuncia 'Dia D' contra Irã e impõe sanções contra pessoas e organizações ligadas ao regime. E o Canadá irá realizar um tarifaço em retaliação às tarifas americanas.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou que esta segunda-feira (24) seria o “Dia D” da guerra econômica que está promovendo contra o Irã. E o Departamento do Tesouro americano de fato anunciou sanções contra pessoas e organizações ligadas ao regime de Teerã e ameaçou fazer o mesmo com países que mantenham qualquer transação econômica com o Irã. O governo iraniano reagiu e afirmou que parceiros comerciais como China e Rússia estão a seu lado. Já nesta terça-feira (25), o Canadá anunciou que irá promover um tarifaço em retaliação às tarifas impostas por Trump aos produtos canadenses – serão alíquotas de até 50% em cerca de 700 produtos importados dos EUA, um impacto de quase R$ 20 bilhões.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery entrevista Cristina Pecequilo, especialista em relações internacionais. Cristina descreve como o primeiro-ministro canadense Mark Carney enfrentou Trump sob a lógica do “dólar por dólar” e os efeitos do atrito para as economias dos dois países. Ela também explica a tentativa americana de sufocar o Irã com sanções comerciais – e o que Teerã planeja fazer como reação.

Convidada: Cristina Pecequilo, doutora em Ciência Política pela USP, professora de Relações Internacionais da Unifesp e comentarista da rádio CBN.

O podcast O Assunto é produzido por: Luiz Felipe Silva, Carlos Catelan, Luiz Gabriel Franco, Juliene Moretti, Stéphanie Nascimento, Marco Antônio Martins e Thomé Granemann. Na apresentação: Natuza Nery.

articles.title: Zelador agredido no DF apresenta melhora, mas segue na UTI | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima foi extubada na sexta; família diz que médicos ainda avaliam retirar traqueostomia. Vanderlei Lima foi agredido na madrugada de 7 de agosto, na 314 Norte.
articles.summary: Vanderlei Souza Lima, zelador agredido no DF, apresenta evolução na UTI e médicos avaliam retirada da traqueostomia para que ele volte a respirar sozinho.
articles.body:
Mais de duas semanas depois de ser agredido com uma paulada na cabeça , o zelador de um prédio na Asa Norte, no Distrito Federal, apresenta evolução no quadro de saúde, segundo a família.

Vanderlei Souza Lima continua internado na UTI do Hospital de Base, mas vem reagindo aos estímulos.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 no WhatsApp.

Maria Bia, prima de Vanderlei, contou ao g1 que o zelador responde a algumas interações – abre os olhos ao ouvir a voz dos familiares e fica agitado durante as visitas.

A família recebeu da equipe médica a informação de que ainda é cedo para fazer um diagnóstico sobre possíveis sequelas .

“Ele está ouvindo, só não está conseguindo falar, mas ele ouve direitinho. Ele entende tudo que a gente fala, está indo muito bem”, disse.

Vanderlei Souza Lima foi agredido por um homem em situação de rua. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

A função dos rins era uma das principais preocupações nos últimos dias. No entanto, o quadro também apresentou melhora.

Vanderlei foi extubado na última sexta-feira (21), segundo a família . Depois, ele passou a respirar com auxílio de uma traqueostomia. Agora, os médicos avaliam retirar a cânula para que ele respire sozinho.

O zelador foi agredido com uma paulada na cabeça na madrugada de 7 de agosto, na 314 Norte. Câmeras de segurança registraram uma discussão entre ele e o agressor, que também aparece com uma faca (veja no início da reportagem).

Segundo a polícia, a discussão teria começado depois que o zelador pediu para que o homem saísse das proximidades do prédio.

Zelador e homem em situação de rua discutem antes de agressão no DF — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

O suspeito, identificado como Alexandre da Trindade Leite , de 45 anos, foi preso no dia seguinte ao ataque. Segundo a Polícia Civil, ele já tinha passagens por roubos e furtos.

O caso é investigado pela 5ª Delegacia de Polícia, na área central de Brasília , como tentativa de homicídio. A Justiça havia expedido um mandado de prisão preventiva contra o suspeito.
