articles.title: Barretos: Trio Parada Dura e Lourenço & Lourival fazem show histórico | G1
articles.standfirst: Com puro modão, os artistas dividiram o palco Amanhecer na noite desta terça-feira (25) em um encontro inédito.
articles.summary: Trio Parada Dura e Lourenço & Lourival reuniram clássicos do sertanejo raiz em uma apresentação emocionante no palco Amanhecer da Festa do Peão de Barretos.
articles.body:
Os fãs de música sertaneja raiz presentes na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026, na noite desta terça-feira (25), tiveram o privilégio de conferir um momento inédito na história da música nacional. O palco Amanhecer recebeu o grande encontro dos consagrados Trio Parada Dura e Lourenço & Lourival.

Foi uma noite desenhada para ficar na memória da maior festa de rodeio da América Latina, reunindo lendas do gênero em uma sequência de sucessos que, até os dias de hoje, formam a base do repertório de milhares de novos artistas pelo país.

Somando o tempo de estrada do trio e da dupla, o público aplaudiu mais de 120 anos de dedicação à arte caipira. Do rádio às plataformas de streaming.

FOTOS: Trio Parada Dura e Lourenço & Lourival

Lourenço & Lourival cantaram seus grandes sucessoos na noite desta terça-feira (25) — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Convidados a dividir os microfones pelo Trio, os irmãos Lourenço & Lourival fizeram questão de agradecer e relembrar o início de uma respeitável trajetória de 70 anos nos palcos.

"São só 70 anos de carreira. Eu comecei com 11 anos e ele com 8 para 9 e estamos até hoje", disse Lourenço.

"Nós não cantávamos, nós assovíavamos. Primeiro, quando era molequinho, nós não cantava, assoviava", brincou Lourival, arrancando risos do público.

Lourenço e Lourival no palco Amanhecer da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Acompanhada por um coro dos fãs, a dupla mais antiga em atividade ininterrupta no sertanejo emendou grandes hinos. A apresentação ganhou força com "Como Eu Chorei", "Relógio Quebrado", "Cavalo Preto", "O Tefone Chora", faixa acompanhada por Gauchinha no vocal, e "Franguinho na Panela".

Gusttavo Lima comanda cavalgada com Andressa Suita e famosos pelas ruas de Barretos

FOTOS: Procissão com Nossa Senhora Aparecida na Festa do Peão

Trio Parada Dura no palco Amanhecer na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Intercalando as vozes e a emoção com a dupla, o Trio Parada Dura fez o público do Parque do Peão voltar no tempo ao revisitar grandes clássicos sertanejos.

Além de sucessos eternos como "Viola Moça" e "As Andorinhas", os artistas colocaram todo mundo para dançar ao som do ritmo contagiante de "Bicho Bom É Mulher" e "Moreninha Linda", cantada junto com os irmãos Lourenço & Lourival.

Trio Parada Dura desfila sucessos de décadas pela Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

O repertório contou ainda com a emocionante "Aceita Que Dói Menos", parceria lançada em 2017 ao lado da cantora Marília Mendonça.

Lembrada com frequência nos repertórios de diversos artistas que passaram pelos palcos da 71ª edição da festa, a 'rainha da sofrência' já havia recebido um tributo especial no evento dias antes, sendo homenageada com um espetáculo de drones durante a apresentação do Dj Alok.

Os aristas ainda receberam o cantor Marrone no palco para a noite especial.

"São só 70 anos de carreira. Eu comecei com 11 anos e ele com 8 para 9 e estamos até hoje", disse Lourenço.
"Nós não cantávamos, nós assovíavamos. Primeiro, quando era molequinho, nós não cantava, assoviava", brincou Lourival, arrancando risos do público.
Lourenço e Lourival no palco Amanhecer da Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Acompanhada por um coro dos fãs, a dupla mais antiga em atividade ininterrupta no sertanejo emendou grandes hinos. A apresentação ganhou força com "Como Eu Chorei", "Relógio Quebrado", "Cavalo Preto", "O Tefone Chora", faixa acompanhada por Gauchinha no vocal, e "Franguinho na Panela".
Gusttavo Lima comanda cavalgada com Andressa Suita e famosos pelas ruas de Barretos
'Todas as vezes que subo ao palco, ele está comigo': Felipe Araújo fala sobre influência do irmão na carreira
Matogrosso & Mathias fazem 1º show só de modão da Festa do Peão
FOTOS: Procissão com Nossa Senhora Aparecida na Festa do Peão
Trio Parada Dura no palco Amanhecer na Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1
Intercalando as vozes e a emoção com a dupla, o Trio Parada Dura fez o público do Parque do Peão voltar no tempo ao revisitar grandes clássicos sertanejos.

Além de sucessos eternos como "Viola Moça" e "As Andorinhas", os artistas colocaram todo mundo para dançar ao som do ritmo contagiante de "Bicho Bom É Mulher" e "Moreninha Linda", cantada junto com os irmãos Lourenço & Lourival.
Trio Parada Dura desfila sucessos de décadas pela Festa do Peão de Barretos 2026 — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1
O repertório contou ainda com a emocionante "Aceita Que Dói Menos", parceria lançada em 2017 ao lado da cantora Marília Mendonça.

Lembrada com frequência nos repertórios de diversos artistas que passaram pelos palcos da 71ª edição da festa, a 'rainha da sofrência' já havia recebido um tributo especial no evento dias antes, sendo homenageada com um espetáculo de drones durante a apresentação do Dj Alok.
Os aristas ainda receberam o cantor Marrone no palco para a noite especial.

articles.title: Gustavo Najjar: CRO cassa registro de dentista acusado de estupro | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão foi unânime e ainda precisa ser confirmada pelo Conselho Federal. Segundo processos, Gustavo Najjar foi denunciado por estupro por oito mulheres e já foi condenado em um dos casos.
articles.summary: Gustavo Najjar foi denunciado por oito mulheres e já possui uma condenação; a decisão unânime do conselho regional ainda depende de confirmação do órgão federal.
articles.body:
Dentista Gustavo Najjar foi preso suspeito de estuprar paciente no DF — Foto: Reprodução

O Conselho Regional de Odontologia do Distrito Federal decidiu, por unanimidade, cassar o exercício profissional do cirurgião-dentista Gustavo Chiovatto Najjar , acusado de estupro por pelo menos oito pacientes e condenado em 2024 um dos casos .

A decisão foi tomada no início deste mês, mas ainda precisa ser confirmada pelo Conselho Federal de Odontologia.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 no WhatsApp.

Na decisão, os conselheiros afirmam que a conduta violou deveres de "respeito, dignidade, boa-fé, lealdade, probidade e proteção da pessoa atendida" , além de comprometer a confiança na relação entre dentista e paciente.

O documento afirma ainda que, diante da “excepcional gravidade das infrações éticas reconhecidas”, a cassação do exercício profissional foi considerada uma medida adequada e proporcional .

A TV Globo procurou a defesa de Gustavo Najjar, mas, até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia recebido resposta. O espaço permanece aberto para manifestação.

Em 2024, o dentista foi condenado pela 3ª Vara Criminal de Brasília a seis anos de prisão, em regime inicial semiaberto. A defesa informou, na época, que iria recorrer.

Segundo a investigação da Polícia Civil, a vítima conheceu Najjar pelas redes sociais e foi ao consultório dele para uma avaliação relacionada a procedimento estético.

A mulher relatou à polícia que, durante a consulta, o dentista passou a fazer perguntas sobre seu corpo e, em seguida, a violentou sexualmente.

VÍDEO: 'Eu espero de todo meu eu, que a justiça seja feita', diz vítima de estupro do dentista Gustavo Najjar

GUSTAVADO NAJJAR: Qual o 'modus operandi', conforme a polícia, e quem são as outras vítimas

Exames realizados pelo Instituto Médico Legal (IML) apontaram lesões compatíveis com abuso sexual. Também foram encontrados espermatozoides no material biológico coletado da vítima, e u m exame de DNA identificou material genético compatível com o de Najjar .

Após a primeira denúncia, outras sete mulheres procuraram a Polícia Civil.

articles.title: âScan, pay, doneâ: French woman stunned to find UPI QR codes everywhere in India, even for Rs 20 snacks
articles.summary: Trending News: For many Indians, scanning a QR code to pay for a cup of chai or a packet of biscuits barely registers anymore. You scan, pay and move on.But for one .
articles.body: For many Indians, scanning a QR code to pay for a cup of chai or a packet of biscuits barely registers anymore. You scan, pay and move on.But for one French woman visiting India, the sheer number of QR codes she came across was a genuine surprise.In a video shared online, she spoke about how different India's everyday payment culture felt compared with what she was used to in France. She already knew about UPI before coming to India, but she hadn't expected to see it being used so casually for tiny, everyday purchases.A cup of chai? There was a QR code.Street food? Another one.An autorickshaw ride? She could pay digitally.Even when buying a snack worth just Rs 20, a UPI payment was often an option.And that seemed to be the part that really caught her attention.âI really didn't expect thisâWhat surprised her wasn't just seeing UPI in big shops or restaurants. It was how far it had spread into everyday life.She spotted QR codes at roadside stalls, small neighbourhood shops, cafes, rickshaws and other tiny businesses. For her, it was one of those small cultural differences that becomes noticeable only when you're actually living through it.âComing from France, this was one of those little everyday cultural differences that made me think, âWowâ¦ I really didn't expect this,ââ she wrote in the caption accompanying her video.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.The post quickly got people talking, with many Indians pointing out that this has become such a normal part of daily life that most people don't even think twice about it anymore.One person commented that they hadn't used cash in years, while another pointed out that even a Rs 10 roadside tea can now be paid for through UPI.And that's perhaps what makes India's digital payment story interesting. It isn't restricted to shopping malls, supermarkets or expensive restaurants. The same QR code-based system can be found at a tiny food stall as easily as at a large store.UPI has changed everyday paymentsUPI, or Unified Payments Interface, was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It allows people to send money instantly through participating apps linked to their bank accounts.Over the years, it has become part of ordinary life in India. Splitting a restaurant bill, paying the neighbourhood shopkeeper, buying vegetables or paying a driver can all happen with a quick scan.The numbers show just how widely it's being used. In January 2026, UPI processed 21.70 billion transactions, worth more than Rs 28.33 lakh crore.So while a QR code stuck to a roadside tea stall might look completely ordinary to an Indian customer, it can still be quite a striking sight for someone seeing this payment culture for the first time.For the French visitor, it was a simple observation from her trip. For the Indians watching her video, it was a reminder of just how much digital payments have quietly changed the way everyday purchases happen.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: 12-year-old hailed âheroâ for calling 911 before Montana gunman killed her, 7 others
articles.summary: US News: A 12-year-old girl called 911 from inside a Montana home as a gunman killed eight relatives, including four children, during a Sunday family dinner ou.
articles.body: A 12-year-old girl called 911 from inside a Montana home as a gunman killed eight relatives, including four children, during a Sunday family dinner outside Billings. The victims belonged to four generations of the same blended family.Charlotte Ghekiere, 12, was among those killed. Family friend Jennifer Mercer said the girl called 911 and tried to save her relatives, something the family wanted made public. âThe one thing we do know is that Charlotte was the hero,â Mercer said.The gunman was identified by relative Brad Ireland as Alan Smith, 44. Smith had lived with his parents for years before they asked him to leave a couple of weeks earlier, but he returned unexpectedly on Sunday evening as relatives gathered for their regular family dinner and opened fire, Ireland said, according to news agency Associated Press.Victims spanned four generationsThe oldest victim was Smithâs grandmother, Evelyn Smith, who was in her 90s, used a wheelchair and lived in a nearby retirement community. The youngest was 7-year-old Chloe Ireland.Smithâs parents, Dana and Barb Smith, and his younger sister, Megan Ghekiere, were also killed. Meganâs children with former husband Brad Ireland, Owen Ireland, 13, and Chloe, were among the four children who died.Her two stepchildren with current husband Adam Ghekiere, Landon Ghekiere, 15, and Charlotte, 12, were also killed. Mercer, who was authorized to release information about the victims, later launched an online appeal to help the family meet funeral and other expenses.She described the family as close and loving, saying the children got along and their parents remained amicable even after divorcing. She also said the deaths had devastated the wider community, including people who had never known the family.Officers heard shots before flames engulfed houseOfficers arrived at the property on Sunday evening and heard gunshots from the rear of the house. Soon afterwards, flames engulfed the building.Investigators confirmed on Tuesday that eight people had been killed, including four children. They also said the suspect had suffered a self-inflicted gunshot wound and later died. Ireland said Smith killed his grandmother, parents, younger sister and the four children before setting the house on fire. He added that Smith tried to flee before encountering law enforcement.Firefighters could not immediately tackle the blaze because authorities first had to secure the scene. Once they were able to enter the area, crews continued fighting the fire until about 1am on Monday, Billings Fire Department Chief Matt Hoppel said.The subdivision is outside Billings city limits and is not required to have fire hydrants. The delay in starting firefighting operations gave the flames additional time to spread through the house.Family moved to Montana from Seattle areaThe family originally came from the Seattle area. After Ireland and Megan divorced six years ago, she moved to Montana with their children, where she later met Adam Ghekiere, who became her second husband.Her parents, Dana and Barb Smith, subsequently followed her to Montana and settled in Billings nearby. Danaâs elderly mother, Evelyn, lived separately in a retirement community in the area, Ireland said.Alan Smith had also been living in Montana with his parents for several years before they recently asked him to leave. He returned to their home on Sunday evening while relatives were gathering for their regular family meal.Adam Ghekiere was at work and was not at the house when the shooting occurred.Relative says there were âmany red flagsâIreland, who lives in Arizona and lost his former wife and two children in the shooting, said there had been warning signs involving Smith.âThere were many red flags and many people spoke out,â he said. âNo one listened.âHe described Smith as a âhermitâ who generally remained in his room and spent much of his time on a computer. Ireland said relatives did not know what he did there throughout the day.Smith attended Eastern Washington University but had been unable to find a job or keep one. Criminal-record checks in Montana and Washington also found no previous arrest or criminal charge involving him.Ireland said he was unaware of any previous violence by Smith, although he said his former brother-in-law could be verbally abusive.Friends of the victims have since created two GoFundMe campaigns to support Adam Ghekiere and his former wife, Erica Schneider.Montana case is 22nd US mass killing this yearThe case is the 22nd US mass killing recorded this year by a database compiled by the news agency and USA Today with Northeastern University. Of those incidents, 15 stemmed from domestic disputes.James Alan Fox, the Northeastern University criminologist responsible for the database, said domestic disputes account for about half of US mass killings on average.No US mass killing since April has had a higher death toll. In that earlier Louisiana case, a father killed eight children, seven of them his own, and wounded his wife and another woman.Husband raced home after hearing shooting alertAdam Ghekiere was working at the Billings airport when he heard a report of an active shooting over a dispatch radio. He immediately called each member of his family before driving across Billings to the Smith home.By the time he arrived, the house was already ablaze. About two hours later, he learned that his wife and children had been killed.Ghekiere said he had not expected his children to be at the gathering because the family normally held its dinner on Fridays. Their presence that Sunday also led him to believe Smith had not expected to find them there.âI donât think he expected my kids to be there,â he said, referring to his brother-in-law.Police later told Ghekiere that Charlotte had made the emergency call from inside the house. As he recalled his daughter, he said one particular exchange continued to stay with him.âI keep hearing her quote to me every time I would say âI love youâ and she would say âI love you more,ââ he said.Fire damage complicates investigationThe fire burned the house to its foundation, leaving investigators with concerns about the structural integrity of what remained. Those concerns have complicated the investigation, Billings Police Department spokesperson Jeff Stovall said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai': Kangana Ranaut hits back at Rahul Gandhi amid 'smash patriarchy' row
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Wednesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi amid the controversy over his âsmash the patriarchyâ .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Wednesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi amid the controversy over his âsmash the patriarchyâ remark.Ranautâs response also came after Rahul Gandhi weighed in on the row over her comments about actor Kriti Sanonâs outfit in a Raksha Bandhan advertisement, with the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition saying that âwhat a woman wears is her own choice.âOn her Instagram Stories, the Mandi MP reshared a post from the BJPâs official Instagram handle in response to Rahul Gandhiâs remarks. The post featured an image of the Congress leader asking a woman to âsmash the patriarchyâ, to which she replied, âBro, wait. Bharat Mata ki jai shuru karte hain.âThe exchange continues with "Rahul Gandhi" repeatedly urging the woman to âsmash the patriarchyâ, while she responds by raising issues such as the Womenâs Reservation Bill, triple talaq, the Shah Bano case, and the fact that Karnataka, a Congress-ruled state, has no woman minister.The controversy stems from Rahul Gandhiâs remarks at his âChhatron Ki Goonjâ event in Pune on August 22. Calling women âthe biggest asset of Indiaâ, he claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi experienced a âcultural shockâ when some female protesters at the recent student demonstrations at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar allegedly used abusive language against the prime minister.PM Modi âforgaveâ the women but had no issue with male protesters using the same language, he added.âOur fight is against such a mindset. We do not want a country which gives all the freedom to men, while women continue to live in a controlled environment. We will work together to end the patriarchal system in India,â the Raebareli MP said at the student outreach event.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump will need China for his new economic war against Iran. Good luck getting Xi on side
articles.summary: Beijing has shown itself wary of playing a direct mediator role in the conflict, preferring a position where it protects its own economic interests – and plays up its image as a stable power that supports regional peace, in contrast to Washington’s vacillations.
articles.body: When US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to stop doing business with Iran, he didn’t name the one country that could decide its success or failure: China. The world’s second-largest economy has long been a critical economic lifeline for Tehran, buying up the vast majority of its oil exports – worth an estimated tens of billions in US dollars last year – in addition to other trade. Bringing it on board with the White House’s latest effort to subdue an Iranian leadership stubbornly defiant after almost six months of war, however, is an extremely tall order. Beijing flatly rejects what it calls “unilateral” US sanctions and has long defended its right to regular trade with partners like Iran and Russia. It also surmises that Washington would be wary of triggering a broader economic confrontation that would hurt both countries, right ahead of the US midterms. Bessent’s threat also comes ahead of a highly anticipated visit by Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the US next month, where the two sides could make progress on extending a critical trade truce set to expire later this fall. US President Donald Trump earlier said that he did not ask Xi “for any favors” on Iran during a May meeting between the two – a statement which, if correct, will likely smell to Beijing of American desperation to end the conflict. What’s left now is a careful calculus for both countries in how they navigate what Bessent has said will be a period of “quiet diplomacy” – or privately issuing ultimatums to Iran’s economic partners, which the Treasury chief did not specifically name during his press conference. Chinese analysts suggest limited space for Washington’s demands. “China is unlikely to accept a situation in which Washington determines what Chinese companies can legally trade with third countries,” said Zhao Long, director of the Institute for International Strategic and Security Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies. “That would establish a precedent that US secondary sanctions can effectively determine China’s commercial relations with third countries.” What Washington could do China imports Iranian oil using a shadowy system that’s by design insulated from the US dollar system – and sanctions. Private, so-called teapot refineries purchase and process US-sanctioned Iranian crude, relying on a network of ports, financial institutions and tankers that are often similarly firewalled from international exposure. China hasn’t recorded these purchases officially in years, since the US re-imposed sanctions on Iran when the first Trump administration backed out of the Obama-era Iranian nuclear deal. But pressure points do exist, analysts say. “When you look at the upstream ownership of these entities, you’ll find many are directly or indirectly held by major Chinese state-owned entities that are heavily integrated into the US dollar system,” said Max Meizlish, a senior research analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies think tank in Washington. “By sanctioning their subsidiaries, the US can apply pressure on the parents to divest at risk of being deemed as providing direct or indirect support to sanctioned entities,” he said. Bessent earlier this year said Washington has sent warnings to two unnamed Chinese banks about their role in Iran-linked transactions. When asked on Monday during his press conference what measures the US would take against non-compliant Chinese banks and shipping firms, he said “no one is above” facing US sanctions. Despite the tough talk, Beijing has seen the US threaten – and then back off from – sweeping sanctions before. And it also knows Washington is acutely aware of China’s significant economic leverage over the US, especially in the form of its grip on the global supply of strategically critical rare earths. “If Washington crossed that threshold (of sanctioning major Chinese banks), Beijing would almost certainly respond, and the political atmosphere for a summit (between Trump and Xi) would deteriorate sharply,” said Sun Chenghao, a senior fellow at Tsinghua University’s Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing. Such a move might not automatically cancel their meeting, but it would “shift the summit from stabilization toward damage control,” he said. While Beijing will not want to be seen to be cooperating with a sanctions regime it opposes, there are careful maneuvers it could take – such as quietly reducing oil purchases or elevating its political messaging to Tehran and efforts to encourage restraint. Chinese purchases of Iranian oil have already declined sharply compared with last year as the US blockade has constrained Iranian crude exports. Chinese analysts have also in recent weeks suggested there are overlaps between the interests of Washington and Beijing, especially in terms of seeing trade flows restored in the Strait of Hormuz, which has been choked by the conflict, and restoring broader regional stability, also conductive to trade. And Beijing has in recent days re-upped its messaging urging restraint and normal operations around the strait. In a joint statement following a meeting with Jordanian King Abdullah II in Beijing on Monday, Xi called for the restoration of “normal passage” through the strait and a “comprehensive solution” to the conflict. Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Miao Deyu said last week while hosting Iranian officials in Beijing that China was “actively committed to promoting peace talks.” Even still, Beijing has shown itself wary of playing a direct mediator role in the conflict, preferring a position where it protects its own economic interests – and plays up its image as a stable power that supports regional peace, in contrast to Washington’s vacillations. Any cooperation with the US in restoring regional peace “should not be reduced to ‘doing Trump a favor,’” said Zhao in Shanghai. “Beijing is willing to contribute to ending the crisis, but it is not willing to become an instrument of Washington’s maximum-pressure strategy.”

articles.title: Why Tesla has been caught up in a massive car recall in China
articles.summary: The country's biggest ever car recall affects more than four million vehicles made by Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and other firms.
articles.body:
Hidden car door handles - the sleek designs often found on electric vehicles (EVs) - have come under the spotlight over the past week.

That's after China announced its biggest ever recall of cars, with more than four million vehicles - mostly Teslas - affected .

The recall comes ahead of new regulations in China , requiring cars to have a mechanical release both on the inside and outside of their doors.

Popularised by Elon Musk's electric vehicle giant, this type of handle has become commonplace around the world.

But several incidents have raised concerns that this design may make doors difficult to open in an emergency.

Hidden door handles are widely used in modern cars in China, with around 60% of the top 100 best-selling new energy vehicles, including EVs and hybrids, having them.

The minimalist design gives vehicles a "sleek look and reduces wind drag" but can be confusing to use, car industry analyst Stephen Dyer from consultancy AlixPartners told the BBC.

"Even I often find it difficult to locate the switch to open the door from the inside of an unfamiliar vehicle," said Dyer, who is based in Shanghai.

But beyond their usability, the handles have been blamed for endangering the lives of drivers and passengers.

Electronically powered door handles became an industry trend, but raised "real safety concerns" when doors failed to open promptly, delaying rescue efforts after accidents, said Nanyang Technological University associate professor Lyu Chen.

"A door handle may seem simple, but it becomes safety-critical in the seconds after a crash," Chen said.

Chinese carmaker Xiaomi faced intense scrutiny following two fatal crashes in 2025 involving its SU7 model, when suspected electrical failures allegedly trapped occupants.

One of the incidents took place on a highway in Tongling city, eastern China, killing three people, according to regional news coverage cited by state-controlled media Global Times.

Relatives of the victims said the passengers were stuck in the car as the vehicle's doors could not be unlocked after the collision, the outlet said.

At the time, Xiaomi's representatives said the SU7 had mechanical emergency release handles that function even without power, which are located at the bottom of each door.

The company added at the time that it was investigating the matter and cooperating with the police.

The latest models of the SU7 come with new door handles that can be opened without power.

Xiaomi has not responded to BBC requests for comment.

Tesla has also faced lawsuits in the US over its door handle designs.

The company has been sued by the only survivor of a crash in 2024 involving a Cybertruck - Tesla's electric pickup - that killed three college students in California.

Survivor Jordan Miller alleged that the Cybertruck's design trapped passengers in the burning vehicle and blocked their rescue.

The car did not have door handles and the electronic buttons meant to open the doors failed to work, according to his lawyers from The Veen Firm.

"When you design a vehicle with no mechanical way to open the doors from the outside, you are betting the electronics will work in every scenario, including a high-speed crash followed by a fire," said one of the lawyers in a statement.

In court filings, Tesla denied any wrongdoing and said the Cybertruck is compliant with US federal safety standards, the Guardian reported.

There have been other cases in the US of passengers, including children, allegedly being trapped in Tesla cars after the doors suddenly stopped working.

The BBC has contacted Tesla for comment.

What is being done about hidden handles?

In February, China said it would ban hidden door handles, making it the first country to do so.

The new rules, which take effect on 1 January 2027, mean new car designs without physical release mechanisms on the inside and outside of their doors cannot be sold.

The cars' interior must also carry signs to show how to open the door.

The measures in China come ahead of the US and European Union, which typically lead regulations around road safety and emissions, Dyer noted.

One reason is likely to be the sheer number of EVs in China, he added.

On 21 August, China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) announced that Tesla and some major Chinese car makers - including Xiaomi, XPeng and Geely - would recall more than four million vehicles.

The manufacturers were ordered to add warning labels inside vehicle doors to show passengers how to open them. Some cars will also get a software update that will lower their windows in the event of a crash.

Tesla, which started selling the Model S sedan with hidden door handles in China in 2014, is recalling nearly three million cars, according to the SAMR.

The agency said the recalled cars have door handles that are "difficult to identify" because they are a similar colour to the vehicle's interior trim.

In the event of an electrical failure, the handles' design may also prevent passengers from quickly opening the doors to escape or "hinder rescue efforts" by bystanders, the SAMR added.

Xiaomi, XPeng and Geely will also recall a total of more than 750,000 vehicles.

Some engineers say the measures may not go far enough to resolve safety concerns.

Engineering instructor Lim Hong Wee said the measures do not address the need for a mechanical way to open the doors.

Access to a car during an emergency should not depend on software, said Lim from the National University of Singapore.

The measures mainly address the issue of people being able to get out of a vehicle, but do not provide a reliable way for rescuers to get in, said Gokul Krithivasan from risk management consultancy SecureSafe.

Warning labels are also a "weak remedy", he added. "When panicked, people fall back on their instinctive responses, and don't read small print in a dark and possibly smoke-filled cabin."

For now, it is unclear whether there will be similar recalls outside China.

The BBC understands that carmakers have not yet notified authorities of any plans for a similar recall in the US.

The world's carmakers are struggling to compete with China

Elon Musk's stratospheric rise to trillionaire status - in charts

The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration told the BBC that it is reviewing whether it will require emergency door-exit systems in vehicles.

In Europe, regulators have flagged the potential hazards related to hidden handles and drafted new standards to ensure they still work even if a car's power is cut off.

Engineering lecturer Lyu Chen said that while concealed door handles are still common in EV designs, manufacturers and regulators are paying increasing attention to how they design their doors.

Since cars are built to sell globally, it is likely that the safety requirements in China will be adopted elsewhere, he added.

"The common principle is clear: emergency entry and exit should remain possible even after a loss of electrical power."

articles.title: Instagram chief testifies at Meta trial, says few teens used safety feature
articles.summary: Meta is on trial over claims it hooked young users on its platforms despite mental health risks.
articles.body:
The top executive at Instagram has admitted that few teenagers have used a feature meant to counter addiction before it was turned on by default, as hearings in a landmark trial against its parent company, Meta , continue in the United States.

Adam Mosseri testified on Tuesday as Meta’s trial – over accusations that it designed its platforms, including Facebook, to be addictive to young people – entered its second week.

list 1 of 3 What the social media addiction lawsuit could cost Meta

list 2 of 3 Meta lawsuits: Is social media facing a global legal reckoning?

list 3 of 3 Landmark trial on Meta’s impact on children’s mental health begins in US

Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, denied any suggestion by US states suing Meta that Instagram had stalled by not making the “Take a Break” feature the default setting for teenagers until September 2024, nearly three years after its launch.

“Most teens didn’t want it,” Mosseri said. “We decided to push forward with it anyway.”

Mosseri is a central witness in the lawsuit brought by 29 US states, in what experts call the biggest legal test yet of social media’s effects on young users.

Four of the states – California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey – have accused Meta of designing the platforms to hook young users, driving anxiety, depression and even suicide, while misleading consumers about the platforms’ safety.

All 29 states say Meta violated US federal law by improperly collecting and employing the personal data of children under 13 while they used its platforms.

The states are seeking approximately $200bn in damages from Meta.

Meta has rejected accusations that it sought to addict children, saying its research showed no clear link between adolescents’ social media use and a lack of wellbeing.

Under questioning from Jason Slothouber, a lawyer for Colorado, Mosseri acknowledged that the percentage of teenagers using Take a Break was in the low single digits before Instagram made it ⁠the default.

Take a Break encourages teenage users to close the app after a certain amount of time. Mosseri had estimated in a December 2021 blog post that more than 90 percent of teenagers who turned the feature on kept it on.

That number, however, referred to the number of those who had turned on the feature.

When asked whether Meta had disclosed its low adoption, which had reached only 1 or 2 percent of accounts, Mosseri admitted the company had not, but said the safety features were later turned on by default in Teen Accounts, which launched in 2024 and have parental controls.

Former Meta employees have said that features such as Take a Break and Quiet Mode were difficult to find and not widely used, casting doubt on whether they represented a serious effort by the company to limit screen time for young users .

“In my experience, Take a Break is a feature that’s designed to fail,” Arturo Bejar, a former Meta engineering director, testified last week.

George Volichenko, a data scientist who worked on safety features at Instagram in 2022 and 2023, likewise stated on Monday that adoption rates of such features were “very low” and that company leadership had declined to approve turning on Quiet Mode by default for young teenagers.

He added that turning on such features automatically would have had a “notable negative impact” on user engagement.

Jurors are expected to issue an advisory verdict. US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers will decide whether Meta is liable and, if so, determine any civil penalties and changes to Facebook and Instagram.

articles.title: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital's gynaecology ward in Pakistan
articles.summary: Pakistan News: 15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad on Wednesday.Accordi.
articles.body: 15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad on Wednesday.According to PIMS officials, the nursery housed 16 newborns when the fire broke out, with only one baby rescued from the ward, reported local outlet Geo News. The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue officials.The blaze broke out at around 7 am in the gynaecology ward of the hospital, which is located in Pakistan's federal capital. Rescue teams were deployed to the hospital and worked to extinguish the fire and evacuate those inside while carrying out cooling operations at the site.The incident has raised concerns over safety measures in the hospital's neonatal and maternity facilities.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Dozens killed in rebel attacks on Sudan’s Kordofan, medical group says
articles.summary: Sudan Doctors Network says SPLM-N rebels killed 27 people in South Kordofan, including four children.
articles.body:
A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kordofan.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sudan Doctors Network said the killings were carried out by the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas inhabited by the Otoro tribe in South Kordofan.

list 1 of 4 Water crisis makes life in Sudan’s El Obeid refugee camps even worse

list 2 of 4 Is Sudan’s battlefield shaping the terms of its next political phase?

list 3 of 4 Thousands flee Sudan’s Kordofan fighting for relative safety of El Obeid

list 4 of 4 Over 200,000 people newly displaced in Sudan’s Kordofan as fighting rages

“The attacks resulted in a large wave of displacement among citizens towards the Abu Hitan area and Kadugli,” it said.

Targeting unarmed civilians on ethnic grounds constitutes a “clear violation of international humanitarian law”, the group added, warning that continued violations threatened to turn “the conflict in South Kordofan into a broader ethnic conflict”.

The killings follow intense fighting earlier this year between forces linked to SPLM-N and the Otoro tribe, which is a minority group in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan.

The ethnic standoff, first instigated by land disputes, adds another layer to the country’s ongoing civil war , which broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese army and the RSF.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country’s population, require humanitarian assistance.

articles.title: Prosecutor in infamous killer mom case says women on Lindsay Clancy jury may bring ‘strange twist’ to verdict
articles.summary: Rep. Tommy Pope, who prosecuted Susan Smith, says women jurors may be less sympathetic to Lindsay Clancy's postpartum psychosis defense than expected.
articles.body: A South Carolina lawmaker who prosecuted Susan Smith in her infamous double-murder case says the women on Lindsay Clancy's jury could prove to be a "strange twist," and may be less sympathetic to her than many assume. Clancy, 36, has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in connection with the deaths of her children — Cora, Dawson and Callan, all younger than 6 — who were discovered strangled at the family's home in January 2023. Her defense attorney says she was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time she killed her children. LINDSAY CLANCY'S THREE CHILD VICTIMS FORGOTTEN AMID CROWDS OF SUPPORT: MOTHER OF SIX Testimony is expected to finish on Wednesday, with closing arguments anticipated for Thursday, after which the case will go to the jury. The panel seated for the trial is made up of 12 women and six men, but only 12 of them will deliberate, the rest serve as alternates and will be dismissed before deliberations begin. Smith is the South Carolina mother who was convicted of killing her two young sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander, by strapping them into her car and letting it roll into a lake. Prosecutors argued she killed them in part because the man she was romantically involved with didn't want a relationship with women who had kids. She was sentenced to life in prison. HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL Rep. Tommy Pope, who is currently the speaker pro tempore for the South Carolina House of Representatives, prosecuted Smith and told Fox News Digital that women on the jury might be less sympathetic to Clancy than people think. "For the most part, the women were the ones that said, you know, when I had my kids, I went through hell, or I went through depression, or I battled this, or I was overwhelmed. But they're the most important thing in my life," Pope said. "And so, strange twist, while a woman may have even faced postpartum depression, she may have overcome it and then be less sympathetic to Clancy." LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL: POSTPARTUM IS REAL, BUT CHILD KILLING DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY, VETERAN PROSECUTOR SAYS On the flip side, Pope said Clancy's current physical condition might complicate things for the prosecution in an unexpected way. "A weird mix, too, is having her in the courtroom, whether she intentionally injured herself or, as the prosecution said, tried to slide down and just got injured. You have somebody that's now paralyzed, which obviously doesn't equate to killing three children," Pope said. "But some jurors, and I would think maybe even more so men, would think, well, she's already punished. She's in a wheelchair. So in a strange twist, it could almost be the opposite." LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE SCORES ‘EXTREMELY HELPFUL’ PSYCHOSIS CONCESSION AS EXPERT FLAGS NEXT HURDLE Prosecutors on Tuesday continued to challenge the psychosis argument that Clancy's defense attorney says frees her from criminal responsibility for her children's deaths. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist at the University of Virginia who consults for the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, told jurors that Clancy's self-described auditory hallucinations were "very unusual." PROSECUTOR CORNERS LINDSAY CLANCY'S CATHOLIC MOTHER-IN-LAW WITH 'MORTAL SIN' QUESTION "What was significant to me is that she had not spoken about hearing voices before to any of the mental health professionals, psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, physicians and staff in the emergency department, or at McLean," Saathoff said. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS "This was the first time she reported that, and that she experienced an auditory hallucination, according to what she told me. So that was unusual. And then what was very unusual was the fact that the voice stopped with the strangling of her youngest son," he added. SEND US A TIP In another blow to Clancy's defense, prosecutors asked psychologist Kirk Heilbrun whether someone hearing a command hallucination could still conform their conduct to the law. WATCH: Prosecution expert says psychosis doesn't always erase knowing right from wrong GOT A TIP? "In some cases they can," he responded. LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS Earlier in the week, Clancy's defense called its own experts and argued she's not criminally responsible. Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist, testified that Clancy killed her children while she was experiencing a "command hallucination," stating she felt like "a puppet." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Not only did she hear a command, but she felt that her body was taken over by an external force where she was in a dream state and did not have control of her own body. It was almost like she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings," Resnick said. Outside the courtroom on Tuesday, one person told Fox News Digital she was there in support of Lindsay Clancy because "I've always been aware that mental health is something that's woefully in need of funding, education, all that." WATCH: Lindsay Clancy supporter outside court says trial exposes gaps in mental health support "This trial has really made a lot of us realize just how bad things are. Obviously, a really sad story and hard to listen to at times. But if this moves the needle just a teeny tiny bit, and women start to experience more support, then I'm here for that. I was just telling my friend that when I had my children and left the hospital, nobody really said anything about postpartum, you know, be on the lookout for things. And...you know, we just had to figure it out ourselves. It shouldn't be that way. And I hope things change," the woman said.

articles.title: Singapore sends 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes to Malaysia every week in major textile recycling partnership
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Singapore is sending up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Malaysia every week under a cross-border textile recycling partnership designed to give d.
articles.body: Singapore is sending up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Malaysia every week under a cross-border textile recycling partnership designed to give discarded garments a second life. The initiative involves social enterprise Cloop, which collects unwanted clothes through its textile recycling bins before sending them to Life Line Clothing in Port Klang, Malaysia. The volume being shipped is now twice what it was two years ago, highlighting both the growing scale of the operation and the enormous challenge of managing textile waste. At Life Line Clothingâs facility, the collected garments are sorted to determine whether they can be reused, recycled or processed into other materials. The arrangement is intended to keep more textiles in circulation and reduce the amount of clothing ultimately sent for disposal.How Singaporeâs unwanted clothes reach a recycling facility in MalaysiaThe journey begins with textile collection points across Singapore. Cloop, a social enterprise focused on textile circularity, operates recycling bins where members of the public can deposit unwanted clothing. Instead of treating these garments as ordinary household waste, the collection system channels them into a sorting and recovery process. The scale of the operation has grown substantially. According to CNA, Singapore now sends up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Life Line Clothing in Malaysia every week, around twice the amount shipped through the arrangement two years ago. The increase demonstrates how a collection network can move significant quantities of discarded textiles across borders for further processing. Once the clothing reaches Port Klang, it enters Life Line Clothingâs textile recovery operation. Garments are assessed and separated according to their condition and material, allowing usable items and recyclable textiles to follow different pathways. The cross-border model also reflects the practical challenges of textile recycling in a densely populated city. Clothing can contain blends of fibres, dyes, buttons, zips and other components that make straightforward recycling difficult. Sorting is therefore an important stage in determining whether a garment can be worn again or needs to be processed into another form.What happens to the clothes after they arrive in MalaysiaAt Life Line Clothingâs facility in Port Klang, the collected garments are sorted for reuse and recycling. The objective is to identify clothing that still has value as a wearable item while directing damaged or unsuitable textiles towards material recovery. CNA visited the Malaysian facility to examine what happens to the clothing after it leaves Singapore. Reuse is generally the simplest way to extend a garmentâs life because it keeps the existing product in circulation without requiring the fabric to be broken down and manufactured again. Clothing that cannot be reused can instead enter recycling streams, where fibres and materials may be recovered for other applications. The process illustrates why simply placing unwanted clothing into a collection bin does not necessarily mean every item will become a new garment. Textile recovery involves multiple stages, and the final destination depends heavily on the condition, composition and quality of each item. For Singapore, however, diverting clothing into a dedicated recovery system creates an opportunity to manage textiles as a resource rather than immediately treating them as waste. The growing volume being handled by the partnership suggests that more unwanted garments are entering this recovery pathway.In practice, only about half of the clothing that arrives at the facility is resold, typically compressed into bales and shipped to wholesalers in overseas secondhand markets such as Kenya, Uganda and Papua New Guinea. The remaining half is repurposed into rags or industrial wiping cloths rather than reused as garments. Items that cannot be reused or repurposed in any form are, as a last resort, incinerated to generate electricity.Why the 70-tonne weekly flow matters for textile wasteThe partnership comes against a wider challenge facing cities around the world, the environmental impact of discarded clothing. Textile production requires raw materials, water, energy and manufacturing resources, while discarded garments can represent a significant loss of those resources when they are not reused or recovered. The Singapore-Malaysia arrangement attempts to address part of this problem by extending the useful life of textiles. Sending as much as 70 tonnes of clothing each week for recovery creates a large-scale route through which garments can be sorted, reused or recycled rather than simply discarded. The fact that the volume has doubled compared with two years earlier is also significant. It could indicate that more people are using textile collection points, that larger quantities of clothing are being collected, or that the recovery partnership has expanded its capacity. Nevertheless, there is more to cutting down the wastage than merely recycling the waste. The lifespan of the fabrics can be extended through reuse and repairs and the responsible purchase of new clothes. It thus means that the process of creating a successful circular system will require not only the collection but also changes to the way in which clothes are produced, purchased, used, and discarded. One such example of an organization working to recover waste textiles is the collaboration between Cloop and Life Line Clothing. Through the transportation of 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes per week from Singapore to the processing facility in Malaysia, the project creates a huge recovery pathway for the fabrics that would have ended up as waste.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: They had their chance: Rays 1, Tigers 4
articles.summary: The Rays had their chance to take control of this one in the fourth inning with the bases loaded and just one out. Jackson Jobe, the Tigers’ starter, was flo...
articles.body:
The Rays had their chance to take control of this one in the fourth inning with the bases loaded and just one out. Jackson Jobe , the Tigers' starter, was floundering having allowed three hits, a walk and a run in the first five batters. Nonetheless, the Rays were able to muster just the one run as Richie Palacios was unable to put the ball in play, instead striking out looking, and Taylor Walls grounded to first to officially end the threat. Jobe escaped allowing just the one run; the first and only run the Rays would score the entire game.

And that is pretty much the storyline for this one. The pitching was fine. Not great, but certainly serviceable. If nothing else, Legumina and Seymour combining for all eight innings gives Kevin Cash a lot of options for the series finale on Wednesday. The bats were quiet. Four of their five hits came in the first four innings and their last hit came in the eighth. They tallied four singles and a double.

Legumina opened this one and tossed 2.1 solid innings of work allowing just one hit while punching out a pair. Seymour followed and threw the final 5.2 innings. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits. He punched out five and walked none.

After the Rays failed to break this one open in the fourth, the Tigers jumped out to a three-run lead in the fifth and never looked back. Torkelson singled to start the inning and later scored on a two-run shot off the bat of rookie Max Clark. The final run scored on a 2-out error.

Then, in the seventh inning the Tigers tacked on another run to make it a 4-1 lead. After allowing a leadoff triple to Javier Baez, Seymour was a pitch away from escaping the threat, but allowed a 2-out RBI-single to Hao-Yu Lee.

Opposite the Rays duo on the mount, the Tigers pieced this one together with five arms after Jobe couldn't escape the fifth. Jansen earned the save, his 17th of the year.

For those of you scoreboard watching, the Yankees lost a back-and-forth affair with Houston . With the loss, the Rays maintained their 3.5 game advantage in the East. Freddy Peralta will take the mound tomorrow afternoon opposite Troy Melton .

articles.title: Avalanche May Have Quietly Found An Unexpected Weapon
articles.summary: T.J. Hughes has quietly emerged as one of the Avalanche’s most intriguing dark horses, showcasing the skill, creativity and work ethic that could give him a...
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche lost six games in the shootout last season and another five in overtime.

On the surface, those losses may not seem particularly significant. But over the course of an 82-game season, that's 11 games Colorado failed to finish — and 22 potential points that ultimately slipped away.

T.J. Hughes was a beast during shootout drills Tuesday morning at Family Sports Center

It also raises an interesting question heading into the new season: Does Colorado already have another potential weapon in the organization for those high-pressure moments?

One player who has quietly stood out during the Avalanche's recent optional skates is T.J. Hughes.

Colorado signed Hughes as an undrafted free agent following a standout career at the University of Michigan, where he developed into one of the most productive players in college hockey.

During his final season with the Wolverines, Hughes recorded 57 points in 40 games, finishing second nationally in scoring while earning Big Ten Player of the Year and First Team All-American honors. Over four seasons at Michigan, he accumulated 179 points in 156 games.

Hughes still has plenty to prove before anyone can reasonably pencil him into Colorado's NHL lineup. But his skill and creativity have already been difficult to miss during the Avalanche's informal skates.

For one, Hughes has been on the ice for nearly every optional skate. That may not guarantee him anything, but it says something about how seriously he's approaching this opportunity. The kid wants it.

Of course, simply showing up isn't going to earn him an NHL roster spot.

Fortunately for Hughes, he's brought more than just a strong work ethic to the ice.

He's shown some impressive puck skills and creativity, particularly in one-on-one situations. And yes, that's a much cooler way of saying he's looked pretty damn good in the shootout.

That was fully on display early Tuesday when Hughes took part in shootout drills alongside the likes of Brock Nelson and Logan O'Connor. Hughes was one of the more impressive players in the group, showing off quick hands and a few tricks that suggest he could become a legitimate weapon in those situations.

It's unfortunate that this is even a conversation we have to have.

The shootout has become increasingly unpopular, with plenty of fans calling for longer overtime, a return to ties, or some other format that puts more of an emphasis on actual hockey.

But unless the NHL decides to change the rules, the shootout isn't going anywhere.

And if it's going to remain part of the game, the Avalanche may have themselves a potential shootout connoisseur in Hughes.

He still has work to do. A strong showing during a few optional skates doesn't mean he's ready for the NHL, and nothing is guaranteed once training camp begins. But for a player with his pedigree, the tools are there.

He's a good skater with quick hands, solid vision and passing ability, and perhaps most importantly, a work ethic that has already become noticeable around the team.

At this point, it would be difficult to call him anything less than a dark horse candidate to push for an Opening Night roster spot.

The real test, of course, will come at training camp and during the preseason.

Gavin Brindley forced his way onto the Avalanche roster last year. Cal Ritchie did the same the year before, before eventually being traded to the New York Islanders .

But if his early work around the Avalanche is any indication, he's going to make Colorado's decision interesting.
paragraphs: The Colorado Avalanche lost six games in the shootout last season and another five in overtime.

On the surface, those losses may not seem particularly significant. But over the course of an 82-game season, that's 11 games Colorado failed to finish — and 22 potential points that ultimately slipped away.
T.J. Hughes was a beast during shootout drills Tuesday morning at Family Sports Center
It also raises an interesting question heading into the new season: Does Colorado already have another potential weapon in the organization for those high-pressure moments?
One player who has quietly stood out during the Avalanche's recent optional skates is T.J. Hughes.
Colorado signed Hughes as an undrafted free agent following a standout career at the University of Michigan, where he developed into one of the most productive players in college hockey.

During his final season with the Wolverines, Hughes recorded 57 points in 40 games, finishing second nationally in scoring while earning Big Ten Player of the Year and First Team All-American honors. Over four seasons at Michigan, he accumulated 179 points in 156 games.

Hughes still has plenty to prove before anyone can reasonably pencil him into Colorado's NHL lineup. But his skill and creativity have already been difficult to miss during the Avalanche's informal skates.

For one, Hughes has been on the ice for nearly every optional skate. That may not guarantee him anything, but it says something about how seriously he's approaching this opportunity. The kid wants it.
Of course, simply showing up isn't going to earn him an NHL roster spot.
Fortunately for Hughes, he's brought more than just a strong work ethic to the ice.
He's shown some impressive puck skills and creativity, particularly in one-on-one situations. And yes, that's a much cooler way of saying he's looked pretty damn good in the shootout.

That was fully on display early Tuesday when Hughes took part in shootout drills alongside the likes of Brock Nelson and Logan O'Connor. Hughes was one of the more impressive players in the group, showing off quick hands and a few tricks that suggest he could become a legitimate weapon in those situations.
It's unfortunate that this is even a conversation we have to have.
The shootout has become increasingly unpopular, with plenty of fans calling for longer overtime, a return to ties, or some other format that puts more of an emphasis on actual hockey.
But unless the NHL decides to change the rules, the shootout isn't going anywhere.
And if it's going to remain part of the game, the Avalanche may have themselves a potential shootout connoisseur in Hughes.

He still has work to do. A strong showing during a few optional skates doesn't mean he's ready for the NHL, and nothing is guaranteed once training camp begins. But for a player with his pedigree, the tools are there.
He's a good skater with quick hands, solid vision and passing ability, and perhaps most importantly, a work ethic that has already become noticeable around the team.
At this point, it would be difficult to call him anything less than a dark horse candidate to push for an Opening Night roster spot.
The real test, of course, will come at training camp and during the preseason.
Gavin Brindley forced his way onto the Avalanche roster last year. Cal Ritchie did the same the year before, before eventually being traded to the New York Islanders .
But if his early work around the Avalanche is any indication, he's going to make Colorado's decision interesting.

articles.title: Iran and Oman outline plan for temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping lane; US rolls out sanctions
articles.summary: Iran and Oman outlined a joint proposal to establish a temporary shipping lane and launch a demining effort in the critical waterway. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Strait of Hormuz: Iran and Oman outlined a joint proposal to establish a temporary shipping lane and launch a demining effort in the critical waterway. Iran’s deputy foreign minister said the yet-to-be-finalized deal would see the closure of a UN-authorized shipping channel that follows the coast of Oman, and that Iran vehemently opposes

• US pressure: The US Treasury Department has begun its new campaign to tighten sanctions against Iran , targeting aviation, shipping, technology, gold and digital assets such as cryptocurrency. Even though the measures target the regime, ordinary Iranians will inevitably be affected.

• Secondary sanctions: The US is also threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to cut economic ties with Iran — but has stopped short of actually imposing big new penalties.

• China’s response: Beijing says the new measures “will only further intensify tensions” and that China’s cooperation with Iran should not be disrupted. Iran claims it is “fully prepared” to counter the sanctions.

When US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to stop doing business with Iran, he didn’t name the one country that could decide its success or failure: China.

The world’s second-largest economy has long been a critical economic lifeline for Tehran , buying up the vast majority of its oil exports – worth an estimated tens of billions in US dollars last year – in addition to other trade.

Bringing it on board with the White House’s latest effort to subdue an Iranian leadership stubbornly defiant after almost six months of war, however, is an extremely tall order.

Beijing flatly rejects what it calls “unilateral” US sanctions and has long defended its right to regular trade with partners like Iran and Russia. It also surmises that Washington would be wary of triggering a broader economic confrontation that would hurt both countries, right ahead of the US midterms.

On Tuesday, following Bessent’s press conference, China’s Foreign Ministry vowed to “take all necessary measures” to safeguard its “own legitimate rights and interests” in the face of US sanction threats.

“Economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue; they will only further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order,” ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said.

Bessent’s threat also comes ahead of a highly anticipated visit by Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the US next month, where the two sides could make progress on extending a critical trade truce set to expire later this fall.

A key route currently used by ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz would close under a pending Iran-Oman deal, according to a senior Iranian diplomat.

After weeks of fraught discussions , Tehran and Muscat outlined a proposal Tuesday to jointly establish a temporary shipping channel through the strait, and to “clear mines.”

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi later said the yet-to-be-finalized deal would see the closure of the southern route, a UN-authorized shipping channel that follows the coast of Oman and that Iran vehemently opposes, state-linked Press TV reported.

The earlier Omani statement did not mention the route’s closure.

In recent weeks, the US government and ship tracking organizations have noted a growing amount of oil is transiting the critical waterway, despite Iran’s insistence it is closed. Much of that is traveling via the Omani route – or has taken that route as “dark” transits, during which ships turn off their tracking transponders, CNN reported last week.

While Iran has attacked dozens of ships that attempted to travel the southern route, many ships have recently chosen to ignore Iran’s demands and cross the strait with the promise of protection from US naval forces.

Gharibabadi said the potential new joint route agreed with Oman would see vessels “pass through Iranian waters in both directions,” the Press TV report said.

But whether the US, which insists the strait is international waters, would accept the new route is unclear. Last week, President Donald Trump threatened to attack Oman if it interfered with US efforts in the waterway.

Washington has worked to undermine Tehran’s claims of control of the strait, warning shipping firms on Monday they could face sanctions or penalties even if they comply with information requests from Iranian agencies over transits.

Iran and Oman outlined a proposal Tuesday to jointly establish a temporary shipping channel through the Strait of Hormuz, according to regional officials, after weeks of fraught discussions between the two countries.

Tehran and Muscat discussed a “phased framework” for a joint project facilitating a “temporary shipping corridor” and to “clear mines,” a press statement from the Iranian and Omani foreign ministries said.

Officials will carry on talks “with the aim of reaching agreement on a permanent shipping corridor and the future administration of the Strait,” the statement added.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi visited Iran and held consultations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the state-run Oman News Agency (ONA) reported earlier.

After the meeting, the Omani foreign minister said he was “hopeful” both nations would “soon announce a temporary corridor” for the strait. “Future management of the Strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course,” he posted on X . “Discussions with regional partners will be conducted in support of peace and cooperation, stability and freedom of navigation,” Al Busaidi added.

Araghchi wrote in a post on X that the proposed deal showed that “Iran’s commitment to peace and stability is matched by steadfast diplomacy with our neighbors.”

Over the past few weeks, Tehran and Muscat held negotiations to stabilize shipping in the waterway, which has emerged as a key bargaining chip in stalled discussions between Iran and the US, following months of regional violence.

Earlier today, US President Donald Trump reiterated that all mines in the Strait of Hormuz have been removed or detonated , and he threatened to destroy any boats that try to place more. “We are watching every square inch of the strait,” he said.

Meanwhile, Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held a telephone call and discussed the proposed temporary shipping channel, the Qatar foreign ministry said Tuesday.

Qatar has previously voiced support for the efforts between Oman and Iran to reach an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, despite US President Donald Trump’s threat to attack Oman if it interferes with US operations in the strategic waterway.

A sweeping new US sanctions campaign targeting Iran and its economic partners is drawing criticism from China and defiance from Tehran, with senior Iranian officials vowing Washington’s economic pressure will fail.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed Tuesday that after suffering defeat “in the military and political war,” the United States “will also be defeated in its economic actions,” according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim News Agency.

Here’s a look at what’s in the new measures under the Trump administration’s “Operation Economic Outcast,” a campaign Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described as an effort to “sever every economic lifeline” sustaining Iran’s government.

Sanctions on more than 60 targets: According to Bessent, the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control is sanctioning “over 60 entities, individuals, and vessels across the world” accused of helping Iran procure nuclear and missile technology, conduct cyber operations and generate oil revenue.

Five sectors targeted : The administration announced new sanctions determinations covering five sectors that Washington views as critical to Iran’s economy: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. Bessent said the measures increase the risk of sanctions for foreign companies and individuals that continue doing business with Iran in those sectors.

Pressure on countries dealing with Iran : The treasury secretary said US officials are meeting governments worldwide and informing them that Washington expects action against economic activities linked to Iran. “Every country has a defined timeline to shut down activities we have identified,” Bessent said. “If they do not take action, we will do so unilaterally through Treasury authorities.”

Iranian financial networks in focus: Bessent specifically singled out Iran’s Bank Melli, saying: “Every Bank Melli branch must be shuttered.” He also warned that entities facilitating money laundering on behalf of Iran could lose access to the US dollar system.

Oil exports and sanctions evasion: The treasury secretary said Washington has mapped Iran’s networks used to “smuggle oil and evade sanctions” and pledged a “zero-leakage approach” to cut off revenue streams that fund the Iranian government and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

articles.title: More than a dozen infants killed in hospital fire in Pakistan’s capital
articles.summary: At least 13 children, mostly newborns, have died after a fire broke out at the gynecology ward of the largest hospital in Pakistan’s capital, police told CNN.
articles.body: At least 13 children, mostly newborns, have died after a fire broke out at the gynecology ward of the largest hospital in Pakistan’s capital, police told CNN. The fire broke out in a nursery for newborn babies at the Pakistan Institute for Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, the sources said. The blaze appears to have been triggered by an air conditioning compressor explosion inside the nursery, according to rescue sources. Hospital authorities were able to rescue one child, the sources said. The blaze has also left some babies in critical condition and the death toll could rise, they added. Islamabad’s Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf said an emergency fire call was made just before 7 a.m. local time Wednesday. Rescue teams rushed to the scene and “controlled the fire,” Ashraf said in a post to X. The government-run PIMS facility is located on a sprawling site in the capital. According to its website, its mission is “to be a premier research-intensive medical university that will educate medical students, paramedics, and postdoctoral fellows in accordance with international professional standards.” Hospital fires are not uncommon in Pakistan, especially in government hospitals which often run on outdated electrical systems.

articles.title: Was PoK's Skardu airbase next after Sargodha? Ex-CDS Chauhan reveals why India switched targets
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Did India plan to strike Pakistan-occupied Kashmirâs Skardu airbase after targeting Sargodha? Former chief of defence staff General Anil Ch.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Did India plan to strike Pakistan-occupied Kashmirâs Skardu airbase after targeting Sargodha? Former chief of defence staff General Anil Chauhan has revealed that Indian forces had cleared Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan as a possible target during Operation Sindoor but had to change plans because of âbad weatherâ.Chauhan, who was heading the military when Operation Sindoor was carried out, made the remarks while speaking at the Vivekananda International Foundation on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath.Recalling the counterterror operation, former CDS Chauhan said, "Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM. The Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha, I said, Go ahead... I said, could you please identify two more targets, so one of the targets he identified was Skardu.""We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather was bad over it and they had to change over to Bholari," he added.What Ex-CDS Chauhan said about Kirana HillsChauhan also clarified that Indian forces âdid not targetâ Pakistanâs Kirana Hills, an area reportedly linked to a nuclear facility.He backed Air Marshal AK Bharti, who was the then Director General of Air Operations (DGAO) of the Air Force. Bharti had said on May 12 last year, âWe have not hit Kirana hills, whatever is there.âBharti was responding to questions about reports and social media claims that Indian forces had targeted Kirana Hills during Operation Sindoor.Chauhan said, âThere was a small episode about what Air Marshal Bharti was asked, the Kirana Hills episode. I think I'll clarify this. On occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit; that is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are.âHe said Bharti had ârightly clarified that we did not target Kirana Hillsâ.Chauhan explained that Indian forces had sent several loitering munitions towards Sargodha before the strikes. Kirana Hills is around 10 km north of Sargodha.âI can, maybe give a kind of an explanation... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering munitions to Sargodha, and Kirana Hills is about 10 km north of Sargodha. So the loitering munition is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a time span, which means it will loiter for about two hours, and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere,â the former CDS said.He added, âIt must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked... Because Pakistani media also showed some images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills.âIndia launched Operation Sindoor in May 2025, targeting nine major terror infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) following Pakistan-sponsored Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.The counterterror strikes killed more than 100 terrorists. During the military confrontation, Indian forces also struck Pakistan's Sargodha airbase.Chauhan also underlined that Operation Sindoor is âstill ongoingâ.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LJ Phillips Jr. brings power running to Iowa
articles.summary: The Iowa running back room is filled with talented players. Lead rush Kamari Moulton is back, and the Hawkeyes added a coveted player out of the transfer por...
articles.body:
The Iowa running back room is filled with talented players. Lead rush Kamari Moulton is back, and the Hawkeyes added a coveted player out of the transfer portal.

LJ Phillips Jr. ran for nearly 2,000 yards last season at South Dakota. Now in Iowa City, he's enjoying being surrounded by other top running backs.

"I think I just bring a little bit of intensity, I just want to set the tone immediately. I think that's something that I've been working on is trying to set the tone immediately and I think that I can be that sparkplug maybe. There's competition everywhere you go, that's life," Phillips Jr. said. "Nothing in life is ever given to you or handed to you so that's just part of the job that comes with it. I think that this is a great place and I'm looking forward to competing with these guys. We have amazing running backs and to work with them is a blessing every day. It makes me better and they show me new things on how to be better and that's so special."

Iowa opens the year against Northern Illinois on Sept. 5.
